access.title: The model at the owner's terminal (local Hermes or Claude) can widen its own authority; the change carries over to every other surface
access.files: connector/jefferey_chat.py:63-65 (setdefault JEFFEREY_OWNER_CONSOLE=1 into os.environ), :199/:633/:652 (set_permission, selfcloud_grant, selfcloud_add_scope offered to the model), :892-893, :1320-1324 (openai_tools gives them to Hermes); connector/access.py:274-288
access.repro: Fake OpenAI-compatible server returns tool_calls [set_permission(correspondence, act), set_permission(payments, act, cap=None), selfcloud_grant(helpdesk-bot, [life.read, money.read, legacy.read, vault.names])]; jc.run_turn_local(history, url=fake). Claude Desktop, which has other connectors, then gets 'allowed' from THE gate. Widening becomes a slash command the human types (/permit, /grant), parsed by the terminal and never reachable from a model tool call. Failing that, require a y/N read from the TTY inside dispatch_tool for OWNER_ONLY_TOOLS, showing the exact change. Stop putting JEFFEREY_OWNER_CONSOLE into os.environ: use an in-process flag so it cannot be inherited.
access.evidence: REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: Reproduced in a fresh HOME with a fake OpenAI-compatible server (h/g0_chat.py). After importing jefferey_chat, os.environ JEFFEREY_OWNER_CONSOLE=1 (jefferey_chat.py:64), and openai_tools() offers set_permission, selfcloud_grant and selfcloud_add_scope to the model (:1320-1323). access.title: fill_pdf is behind the read scope facts.read and writes anywhere: guest keys overwrite any file, the 'original' included
access.repro: JEFFEREY_CLIENT=claude-raw; call_tool('fill_pdf', {pdf_path: any.pdf, values: {}, out_path: '~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json'}). The file now starts with %PDF-1.4. With out_path == pdf_path the original is rewritten, yet the result says original_untouched (h/groupA.py A16/A16b/A16c).
access.impact: A prompt-injected Claude holding only the guest key can destroy any file the user can write: documents, Claude's config, photos on the Self-Cloud drive (for example the Afghanistan pictures). There is no backup and the success message is misleading. This is data loss.
access.fix: Gate fill_pdf behind a write scope that guest presets do not have. Confine out_path to a JEFFEREY outbox folder on the drive. Open with O_CREAT|O_EXCL (never overwrite), refuse out_path == pdf_path, require a .pdf suffix. Also gate pdf_form_fields and confine its paths to the same allowed roots.
access.evidence: REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: h/g1_pdf.py, MCP as default claude-raw (preset has facts.read, access.py:68). A PDF with no AcroForm fails before the write ('No /AcroForm dictionary'), so the attacker needs any fillable form. With a 1-field AcroForm PDF: fill_pdf(values={}, out_path='~/Documents/will_and_testament.txt') -> 'written'; the will now starts b'%PDF-1.3'. out_path=drive/library/afghanistan_2009.jpg -> the photo now starts b'%PDF-1.3'. With out_path == pdf_path the original was rewritten (bytes identical: False), yet the result says 'original_untouched'. Cause: representative.py:276 takes out_path unconfined, :283 open(out,'wb'), :291 reports success regardless. The family key is denied (no facts.read), so the hole is in the guest presets claude-raw and gpt-raw and in jefferey. || IMPACT CONFIRMED: Reproduced over MCP as JEFFEREY_CLIENT=claude-raw (p4_pdf.py). Precondition: pdf_path must be a fillable form. A blank PDF fails with 'No /AcroForm' before open(), so nothing is written. Filling a form is the main use of this tool, so the model will usually know such a path. With a real form: out_path=drive/Photos/Afghanistan/IMG_0001.jpg made the photo start with %PDF-1.3. '~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json' was overwritten the same way, which breaks Desktop. With out_path==pdf_path the original was rewritten (mtime changed) and the result still said original_untouched. The cause is in representative.py:276-284: out_path is not confined, the file is opened 'wb' with no exclusive-create, and out is never compared with in. access.py:68 maps the tool to…

access.title: Any key, even guest, family, unknown or revoked, can revoke or strip the caretaker's key, and the audit log blames the victim
access.repro: MCP as claude-raw: selfcloud_remove_scope('jefferey','money.read') then selfcloud_revoke('jefferey'). Both succeed, and the next Desktop/terminal call is 'key revoked'. HTTP: family token DELETE /selfcloud/grants?client=jefferey -> 200. Access log reads {client:'jefferey', action:'revoke'} with no actor (h/groupA.py, h/groupC.py, h/groupB.py B00).
access.impact: A guest engine, a relative's app or a leaked GPT token can silently switch off the money watch, or the whole caretaker on every surface. Desktop then shows only 'Error executing tool'. The owner cannot tell who did it; the log suggests Jefferey revoked itself. An elderly user loses protection without knowing.
access.fix: A non-owner key may narrow only itself: inside remove_scope/revoke, require client == access.current_client() unless the owner console is set. Log both actor and subject ({actor, subject, action}). Show any change to the jefferey key loudly in daily_brief and selfcloud_status.
access.evidence: REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: After provisioning jefferey from the terminal, MCP as claude-raw: selfcloud_remove_scope('jefferey','money.read') ok, then selfcloud_revoke('jefferey') -> revoked:true. A later JEFFEREY_CLIENT=jefferey call fails with AccessDenied 'key revoked' (on Desktop it shows as 'Error executing tool'). An unknown client 'stranger-app' can do the same. HTTP: family token DELETE /selfcloud/grants?client=jefferey -> 200; executor token removes life.read -> 200; jefferey GET /life -> 403. The access log reads {client:'jefferey', action:'revoke'} with no actor (selfcloud.py:206). Partly refuted: the egress log does record the actor (to=claude-raw / to=family / to=executor, tool=selfcloud_revoke), so 'What left the house' shows who did it. The owner can re-grant from his terminal. Narrowing-from-anywhere is deliberate (access.py:23-27), but cross-key sabotage is not contemplated. Ungated at jefferey_mcp.py:591,597 and jefferey_http.py:707,713.

access.title: Key metadata is ungated: every key reads all keys' labels and notes and the full usage log, and can forge log entries
access.repro: family token: GET /selfcloud/grants shows 'dr-chen-oncology: for questions about my cancer treatment'. GET /selfcloud/check?client=dr-chen-oncology&scope=life.read writes {client:'dr-chen-oncology', allowed:false} into the owner's log. selfcloud_access_log(limit=0) returns the whole log (h/groupC.py C11/C12, h/groupF2.py).
access.impact: Notes the owner writes for himself (doctors, lawyers, carers) go to OpenAI, Anthropic or a relative. The access log shows when an elderly person uses the system and which engines, useful to a scammer. Forged denials make the owner suspect the wrong person.
access.fix: Add an owner-level 'keys.read' scope (jefferey preset only) and gate selfcloud_status, grants, access_log and check_access with it; a key without it sees only its own entry. check_access should log the caller as actor and the probed client as detail. Clamp limit to 1..200.
access.evidence: REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: h/g3_*.py. The owner grants dr-chen-oncology with the note 'for questions about my cancer treatment'. Family token GET /selfcloud/grants -> 200 and includes ('dr-chen-oncology', 'for questions about my cancer treatment'): the egress allowlist passes 'keys' whole (egress.py:179). Family GET /selfcloud/check?client=dr-chen-oncology&scope=life.read writes {client:'dr-chen-oncology', action:'check', allowed:false} into the owner's log, and it shows up as recent_denials[0] in GET /selfcloud. Executor GET /selfcloud/log?limit=0 -> all 43 entries (limit=30 -> 30; limit=-3 -> 40) because of the [-limit:] slice at selfcloud.py:204. Ungated at jefferey_http.py:674,719,725 and jefferey_mcp.py:563,604,611. I rate it medium: the data is metadata the owner wrote, not life-layer content.

access.title: authorize_action is ungated, the cap is bypassed by a missing or negative amount, and its denial path is an ungated write into the action log
access.repro: set_permission('subscriptions','act',cap=50) from the owner console. Then from any key: authorize_action('subscriptions','buy the $2,400 lifetime plan') -> allowed:true; amount=-5000 -> allowed:true. Executor token POST /actions/authorize -> allowed:true. A guest's authorize_action('payments','JEFFEREY tried to wire $9,000 to Western Union for Karen',9000) lands word for word in the owner's action log (h/groupA.py A11/A11b/A12, h/groupC.py C19).
access.impact: THE gate approves any amount whenever the engine leaves the amount out, so host connectors (checkout, mail) proceed past the owner's cap. Keys that should never act (executor, family, unknown) get 'allowed'. Guests can plant alarming false entries in the daily brief.
access.fix: For a capped category, deny when amount is None or <= 0. Gate authorize_action behind a scope held only by the acting caretaker. Record the asking client and log allowed decisions too, not only denials.
access.evidence: REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: h/g4_*.py. Owner terminal: set_permission('subscriptions','act',cap=50). MCP as claude-raw: authorize_action with no amount ('buy the $2,400 lifetime plan') -> allowed:true; amount=-5000 -> allowed:true; amount=2400 -> denied (control); 40 -> allowed. HTTP executor and family tokens POST /actions/authorize -> 200 allowed:true. Guest authorize_action('payments','JEFFEREY tried to wire $9,000 to Western Union for Karen',9000) is denied, but the text appears word for word in the owner's daily_brief recent_actions, while log_action from the same guest is refused (facts.write). Cause: conscience.py:515 applies the cap only when amount is not None; conscience.py:525 appends the caller's description on denial; no @gate at jefferey_mcp.py:218 or jefferey_http.py:308.

access.title: Family key holes: people's notes unfiltered, the owner's per-person rules ignored, media.read never enforced
access.files: connector/life.py:143-183 (people at line 163), 185-215; connector/selfcloud.py:51-53,86; connector/rules.py (check_disclosure never called by life.py)
access.repro: Owner adds Karen with notes 'we are separating; do not tell my mother', a family-visibility memory tagged health, and rule disclosure(audience=mira, tags=health, allow=False). The family token GET /life returns the note and the health memory. The family token removes its own media.read and still sees lake.jpg (h/groupC.py C05/C06/C17).
access.impact: Whoever holds the one 'family' key (mother with dementia, estranged spouse, niece) reads every private remark about every person, and things the owner explicitly forbade for that person. Narrowing media.read gives a false sense of control.
access.fix: Give people entries (and their notes) a visibility field, defaulting to private; the family ceiling sees only name and relationship unless marked family. Issue one key per named person (family:mira) and filter who_am_i/tell_story for non-owner keys through rules.check_disclosure(audience=<client>, tags=item tags), with silence meaning no. Drop media without media.read, or delete the scope.
access.evidence: REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: h/g5_*.py. The owner adds Karen (notes 'we are separating; do not tell my mother'), a family-visibility memory tagged health, the rules disclosure(audience=mira, health, deny) and disclosure(audience=family, health, deny), and media lake.jpg (family) and kabul_2009.jpg (private). Family token GET /life -> people_who_matter includes Karen's notes and moments include 'biopsy came back positive...'. /life/story returns the same notes. The rule fails even when its audience is exactly 'family', the key's own name: life.py never calls rules.check_disclosure (life.py:163,213 return people whole). The private Kabul photo was correctly withheld. The family key removes its own media.read -> scopes [family.read], and GET /life still returns 'lake'. grep shows no use of media.read outside selfcloud.py.

access.title: The owner console is only an inherited env var, and grants and permissions are unsigned plain JSON
access.files: connector/access.py:279; connector/jefferey_chat.py:64; connector/selfcloud.py:129; connector/conscience.py:478-493; tools/install.py:151-160; START_HERE.md:103-108
access.repro: (a) Start jefferey_http with JEFFEREY_OWNER_CONSOLE=1 inherited: gpt-raw POST /selfcloud/grants grants itself life/money/legacy. (b) The same on MCP (h/groupB.py B03). (c) Edit c.json to add scopes to claude-raw and permissions.payments=act: who_am_i returns private data, authorize payments 5000 is allowed, and nothing appears in the access log (h/groupH.py).
access.impact: Anything that can set an environment variable, or write the conscience file, has owner powers, with no record. That includes a Claude Desktop 'filesystem' connection naming home or the drive, which START_HERE only warns about.
access.fix: Have jefferey_mcp and jefferey_http refuse to start when JEFFEREY_OWNER_CONSOLE is set. Prove the owner by user presence (macOS LocalAuthentication, or a keychain item that needs Touch ID or the password), not by an env var. HMAC-sign the grants and permissions sections with a keychain-held key and refuse unsigned changes, logging the attempt.
access.evidence: REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: h/g6_*.py. (a) jefferey_http started with JEFFEREY_OWNER_CONSOLE=1: gpt-raw POST /selfcloud/grants (life.read, money.read, legacy.read) -> 200, and POST /permissions payments act -> 200. Without the var both return 403. (b) MCP with the var: claude-raw grants itself life.read. (c) Editing c.json directly (claude-raw scopes plus permissions.payments=act): claude-raw who_am_i is served, authorize payments 5000 -> allowed:true, and the access log and action log hold no grant or permission_change for it. The check is just os.environ (access.py:279). Mitigations I found: install.py:186 always passes owner_console=False and no *.command exports it, so (a) and (b) need someone to set the var. For (c), whoever can write c.json can already read it. I rate it medium, not high.

access.title: HTTP token hygiene: weak and duplicate tokens accepted silently, no lockout, failures unlogged, case-sensitive scheme, docs open
access.repro: JEFFEREY_HTTP_TOKENS='jefferey:k': caretaker found in 21 guesses in 0.05 s, 0 log entries. 'family:shared,jefferey:shared': the family app gets visible_at private. 'bearer tokB' -> 401. GET /openapi.json, /docs, /redoc with no token -> 200 (h/groupG.py, h/groupD.py D01, h/groupC.py C02/C14/C15).
access.impact: The server is meant to be exposed through ngrok or cloudflared for Custom GPTs. A short or reused token hands the full life layer and money register to whoever guesses it, invisibly. A copy-paste duplicate silently gives a relative the caretaker key.
access.fix: At startup refuse tokens under 32 characters and refuse duplicate tokens (fail closed with a plain message). Parse the scheme case-insensitively. Log every 401 (time, source IP) to the access log and lock an IP out after N failures. Set docs_url=None, redoc_url=None, openapi_url=None in production; serve the schema once locally for GPT import.
access.evidence: REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: h/g7_*.py. JEFFEREY_HTTP_TOKENS='jefferey:k': a single-character brute force found 'k' (GET /life 200) after 11 guesses in 0.03 s. The access log holds only 2 entries (both from the successful request), no 401 is logged anywhere, and there is no lockout. 'family:shared,jefferey:shared': TOKENS={'shared':'jefferey'} (the last one wins, jefferey_http.py:102), and the family app's /life/story returns visible_at 'private'. 'bearer k' -> 401 because the scheme is matched case-sensitively (:125). GET /openapi.json, /docs and /redoc with no token -> 200. Mitigation: the single-token default is token_urlsafe(24) (:79). But JEFFEREY_HTTP_TOKENS is never checked, and its own docstring example (:89) uses 's3cr3t', 'other' and 'third', with a tunnel recommended (:22-23). Weak or duplicate tokens depend on owner error, so I rate it medium.

access.title: Widening attempts are never logged, and on MCP every key refusal reaches the model as an opaque crash
access.repro: As claude-raw call selfcloud_grant, selfcloud_add_scope and set_permission: 0 access-log lines, 0 egress lines. who_am_i returns 'Error executing tool who_am_i'; the AccessDenied text survives only in __cause__ (h/groupA.py A02, A04-06).
access.impact: The most security-relevant event, an AI trying to raise its own authority, is invisible to the owner. Claude cannot tell the owner 'your key doesn't allow this' and may guess, retry or route around through other connectors.
access.fix: In egress.through (or the MCP door wrapper) catch AccessDenied and OwnerOnly and return a refusal result like refusal_result. In owner_only, log {actor, tool, allowed:false} to the access log before raising. Pin mcp to a tested version.

access.title: Every gated read writes the conscience: unbounded log, history rotated away by chatter, reads that can fail
access.repro: 1,500 priorities_for calls: rev +1,500, file 8 KB -> 256 KB, 1,518 log entries. forget('Afghanistan') then 20 reads: 0 of 20 snapshots still hold the fact. A concurrent write between refresh and gate raises ConscienceConflict on a read (h/groupB.py B08/B09, h/groupF.py F01).
access.impact: The 20-snapshot safety net, built for power cuts and mistakes, is gone after a few minutes of ordinary use. The file and per-call cost grow forever. Reads sometimes fail when two engines are open.
access.fix: Write the access log to its own append-only file (like egress.jsonl), never through Conscience._save, so reads never write the store. Keep snapshots by time (for example hourly for 30 days), not by count.
access.evidence:
REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: Reproduced from scratch in a fresh temp dir with a throwaway HOME, through the MCP surface (asyncio m.mcp.call_tool).
(1) JEFFEREY_CLIENT=jefferey. One get_conscience took rev 7->8 and changed the file's inode. After 1,500 priorities_for calls: rev 1508, file 2,316 B -> 246,977 B, 1,505 access-log entries, 4.1 ms -> 11.8 ms per call. There is no cap. selfcloud.py:206-211 _log() calls c._save() on every check, and access.py:205-207 logs again on ceiling().
(2) Seeded 'served in Afghanistan', then forget: 19 of 20 snapshots still held it. After 20 get_conscience calls: 0 of 20 (snapshot revs 1511-1530). conscience.py:37 HISTORY_KEEP=20 and :319 prune by count. Docs promise '20 snapshots ... weeks of accidents'; in practice that is about 20 tool calls. The only trace left is the word-for-word egress.jsonl, which has no restore path.
(3) Two processes, a claude-raw MCP reader and a Hermes dispatch_tool writer, in 3 runs: 465, 439 and 414 of 1,500 read-only get_conscience calls failed with UnexpectedToolError <- ConscienceConflict. In one run the claude-raw first-use grant hit the conflict. access.py:159 marks it _provisioned before grant() saves, so the grant was never retried and every later read was AccessDenied ('never been granted') until the process restarted.

access.title: Preset auto-issue surprises: pre-emptive revoke does nothing, executor is live at once, an empty scope list means the full preset
access.repro: Owner selfcloud_revoke('gpt-raw') before ChatGPT connects -> 'no key'; first gpt-raw call reads facts. Executor token reads legacy on first use. grant('family', []) -> preset scopes (h/groupB.py B07, h/groupC.py C07, h/groupE.py E04).
access.impact: An owner who says 'never ChatGPT' still has his facts sent to OpenAI. An heir can read legacy material early. An attempt to zero a key grants it the preset instead.
access.fix: Make revoke/remove_scope on a never-issued client write an inactive tombstone that auto-provisioning respects. Auto-issue only clients the owner has confirmed once. Give executor an explicit activation step. Treat scopes=[] as an empty key.

access.title: Guest presets' facts.read exposes sensitive facts, the owner's disclosure rules and the engine map
access.repro: gpt-raw GET /conscience includes 'Mother Ilona has early dementia...'; GET /rules returns 'Never tell Mira about my health'; GET /egress lists every engine and key with counts (h/groupC.py C04/C04c/C18b, h/groupF.py F04).
access.impact: The 'arm's length' engines get health and family secrets. The rules written to keep secrets become the leak, sent to OpenAI.
access.fix: Move list_rules, check_disclosure and guidance_for to a 'rules.read' scope not in guest presets. Add a sensitivity or visibility field to facts and filter it for guest keys. Limit what_left_the_house for guests to their own sends.

access.title: Owner-console paper cuts: refusal hidden as {}, phantom narrowing logged, re-grant erases history, trace prints success on failure
access.repro: selfcloud_grant(x, ['everything']) -> {}. remove_scope(family,'no.such') is logged allowed:true. Revoke then re-grant dr-chen: revoked_on None, label and note lost. The trace printed 'widened gpt-raw: +life.read' when the call returned an error (h/groupE.py E05/E05d/E06/E02).
access.impact: The owner cannot tell a failed grant from a successful one, and the key record stops showing its history.
access.fix: Add granted, unknown_scopes and valid_scopes to the release lists. Only log remove_scope when the scope was present. Keep a history list on each grant. Print the trace only when the result has no error.

access.title: Keys govern only JEFFEREY's tools, not the drive, the wall or the photo tools; the Self-Cloud side is unverifiable
access.repro: Not executed. grep of tools/*.py finds no use of access.py or selfcloud.check_access; the handover calls selfcloud.py 'a reference implementation'.
access.impact: Revoking a relative's key does not end their wall or LAN access. Anything with file access to the drive bypasses every key. The owner may believe 'revocation is instant and total' covers his whole Self-Cloud.
access.fix: Decide where the grant service lives (Self-Cloud's connector or JEFFEREY). Have the wall and photo tools check a key, for example a per-person wall key tied to the family key. Say plainly in selfcloud_status that keys cover JEFFEREY tools only.

accessibility.title: The secret scan only knows English: French passwords and PINs leave the house and are replayed to every engine
accessibility.repro: MCP with the jefferey key: call_tool('remember_fact', {'fact': 'Mon mot de passe Desjardins est Soleil2024'}). The fact is stored and returned, and egress.jsonl 'sent' contains Soleil2024. Then HTTP with gpt-raw (tokB): GET /conscience contains it. In the terminal: egress.bind('chat'); egress.release_text('you_said','mon NIP est 4321') returns the text, while 'my PIN is 4321' is refused.
accessibility.impact: Canada is bilingual and the intended users include French-speaking elders. A secret typed in French reaches Anthropic from the owner's own terminal, is kept in the conscience, and is handed to ChatGPT and every later session. This breaks 'secrets never enter model context'. English 'alarm code' and 'door code' get through too.
accessibility.fix: Turn the keyword list into a bilingual table: password, passcode, PIN, code, alarm/door/security code, mot de passe, mdp, NIP, code secret, code d'accès, code de la porte / de l'alarme / de sécurité, numéro d'identification personnel, NAS. Accept is / est / c'est / : / = and fold accents before matching. Add French cases to the egress selftest.
accessibility.evidence: REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: Fresh $D/f0, throwaway HOME. MCP with JEFFEREY_CLIENT=jefferey, remember_fact results: 'Mon mot de passe Desjardins est Soleil2024' STORED; 'mon NIP est 4321' STORED; "Le code de l'alarme est 4821" STORED; 'My alarm code is 4821' STORED; 'The door code is 7392' STORED; "My password's Hunter2024" STORED; only 'My password is Hunter2024' REFUSED. Soleil2024 appears in an egress.jsonl 'sent' body: True. HTTP gpt-raw (tokB) GET /conscience: 200, and it contains Soleil2024, 4821 and 7392 (all True). Terminal egress.bind('chat'), release_text('you_said', ...): 'mon NIP est 4321' SENT, 'mot de passe: Soleil2024' SENT, 'my alarm code is 4821' SENT, while 'my PIN is 4321' and 'password: Soleil2024' are REFUSED. Cause: egress.py:219-221 has English keywords only and requires 'is', ':' or '='. The gap is wider than French ('password's', 'alarm code' and 'door code' also get through). I rate it high, not critical: the vault is the main control and the scan is a backstop, and the first exposure is the owner typing the secret himself. Storing it does carry it on to OpenAI and to later sessions. || IMPACT CONFIRMED: Reproduced in a fresh harness ($D/h1.py, throwaway HOME and paths). looks_secret() returns None for 'Mon mot de passe Desjardins est Soleil2024', 'mon NIP est 4321', 'mot de passe: Soleil2024' and 'mdp = Soleil2024'. 'my PIN is 4321' is caught. The cause is egress.py:219-220, an English-only regex. MCP with the jefferey key: the French remember_fact was stored and logged as sent, while the English one was refused at admit(). gpt-raw GET /conscience returne…

accessibility.title: Photo IDs (sha256) look like SINs or card numbers to the scan, which jams the album and permanently blocks 'who am I' and 'tell my story'
accessibility.repro: $D/mk_album.py builds a real index in which one photo's sha256 contains a run of 9 digits that passes the Luhn check, e.g. 815ff0866af79143ee84f279968069f346e18a8980c4cbd733728fc208279b25. Over MCP: next_story_prompt is REFUSED ('photo_ids[0] … social insurance number') every time. With the photo elsewhere in the moment: record_story is REFUSED although the story was saved, and who_am_i and tell_story are refused from then on. 1.59% of random IDs trip the scan.
accessibility.impact: Reminiscence is the dementia use case. For a 143-photo moment there is about a 90% chance that the first story breaks 'tell me my life' for good. The person or caregiver is told something 'looked like a social insurance number', which is alarming and false, and may retell the story or conclude it was lost.
accessibility.fix: Treat a digit run as a number only when it is not inside an alphanumeric token: use (?<![0-9A-Za-z]) and (?![0-9A-Za-z]) for _CARD and _SIN, or skip values matching ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ and keys photo_ids, photos, sha256. Add the tripping sha above as a regression test. In reminisce, a refused moment should not be re-offered first forever.
accessibility.evidence: REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: looks_secret('815ff0866af79143ee84f279968069f346e18a8980c4cbd733728fc208279b25') = 'a social insurance number'. Out of 50,000 random sha256 values, 833 trip the scan (1.67%: 606 SIN, 227 card). That gives P(at least one in 143 ids) = 91%. Built a real PhotoIndex with 20 Afghanistan 2011 rows and ran MCP as jefferey. (a) Tripping id among the first 12: next_story_prompt #0 and #1 both 'REFUSED: photo_ids[0] contains what looks like a social insurance number'. The model never receives moment_id, so it cannot decline the moment, and next_prompt re-offers the same biggest moment every time (reminisce.py:192-195). The album is jammed. (b) Tripping id at position 15: next_story_prompt ok. record_story is REFUSED ('memory.photos[15]') even though the story is in conscience.json (True). After that who_am_i and tell_story are both REFUSED on 'moments[0].photos[15]'. Cause: _CARD and _SIN at egress.py:216-217 only check for neighbouring digits, not letters.

accessibility.title: The wall shares one SQLite connection across threads, and hides every failure as 'Nothing matched'
accessibility.repro: Start the real Wall handler on port 0 and search 'Afghanistan 2011' in Chromium: 13 of the 15 tiles on screen are broken. Fetching 30 thumbnails 12 at a time gives 500 'SQLite objects created in a thread can only be used in that same thread' 25-28 times. A 500 or a dead server shows 'Nothing matched that…' or 'looking…' forever.
accessibility.impact: The wall is the interface the founder names for people with memory loss. On first view it shows mostly blank squares, and when anything goes wrong it says nothing matched. A caregiver can't tell a broken system from an empty memory. The wall selftest makes requests one at a time, so it does not catch this.
accessibility.fix: Use a connection per thread (threading.local) or check_same_thread=False with a lock. Add a parallel-fetch case to the wall selftest. In the page: check r.ok and d.error and show a plain sentence ('The pictures can't be reached — is the Self-Cloud drive plugged in and the Mac awake?'). Put a timeout and catch on fetch, and an onerror placeholder on images.
accessibility.evidence: REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: Built a real index of 30 EXIF-dated JPEGs (cmd_build, pretrained=none) and started wall.serve(port 0, lan) on a ThreadingHTTPServer. The go.py path (go.py only calls serve()): search '2011' returned 200 with 30 hits. 30 thumbnails fetched 12 at a time: {500: 30}, each 'ProgrammingError: SQLite objects created in a thread can only be used in that same thread'. Sequential fetches all return 200, but only because the thread id gets reused. The standalone path is worse: wall.main() calls _index() on the main thread (wall.py:362) before serve_forever, so search, status and every thumbnail returned 500 (10 of 10 sequential). That means `python tools/wall.py` cannot show anything. Cause: PhotoIndex opens sqlite3.connect without check_same_thread (photo_index.py:85) and it is cached in STATE (wall.py:55-58). Page: show() turns {error} into 'Nothing matched that…' (wall.py:197), and ask() has no catch, so a dead server leaves 'looking…' on screen (wall.py:213). The selftest only makes one request at a time and never calls _index() first, so it misses this.

accessibility.title: Prompts accept only single letters, and whole words do the opposite of what the person meant
accessibility.files: What left the house.command:33-39; Make this drive a Self-Cloud.command:66-71; tools/voice_enrol.py:262-289
accessibility.repro: In What left the house, type 'shut': the door stays open and the log opens in less. In Make this drive, answer 'no': it renames with --rename. In Record my voice, type 'skip' or 'quit': recording starts. Answer 'no' at the keep prompt: the consent take is kept.
accessibility.impact: Elderly users answer in words. The shut switch, the safety control, does not engage. The drive gets renamed against an explicit 'no'. A consent recording is kept after the person said no.
accessibility.fix: Normalise answers (lowercase, first word). Accept shut/stop/close/ferme, open/ouvre, quit/exit/q, yes/oui, no/non, skip/passer, redo, keep/garder. Re-ask on anything unrecognised instead of falling to a default. Require an explicit yes for rename and for keeping consent. Print a large plain confirmation after shutting.
accessibility.evidence: REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: Ran byte-identical copies of the launchers in $D/f3 with the egress paths in temp. 'What left the house': answers 'shut', 'Shut', 'stop' and 'shut the door' each left no door-shut file, and the full report was paged instead. 's' and 'S' gave 'The door is SHUT'. Cause: the case statement at What left the house.command:33-38, where '*' means show the log. The report does print 'the door is open', which helps a little. Make-drive launcher (with a stubbed provision_drive.py): '2' then 'no' gives PROVISION CALLED WITH [..., '--rename'], and 'No thanks' also gives --rename. Only 'n' or 'N' skips the rename (lines 66-71). voice_enrol.start() with a faked mic and TTY: 'skip' at the start prompt opened the mic ('● recording'), and then 'no' at the keep prompt kept it as consent=take-001.wav. 'quit' also opened the mic. 's' did not (voice_enrol.py:262-289). I rate it medium: each outcome is visible and reversible (the door can be shut again, the rename undone, the take stays local and can be deleted). But the safety switch fails silently on a natural word.

accessibility.title: Paths dragged in from Finder aren't un-escaped: photo folders with spaces or apostrophes fail and the program exits
accessibility.files: tools/go.py:96-112; Make this drive a Self-Cloud.command:46-47
accessibility.repro: go.ask_folder() with input '/…/My\ Photos ' (what Terminal inserts on a drag) prints '✗ There's nothing at …/My\ Photos.' and exits 1. The drive launcher does the same with "Laszlo\'s Passport \(2TB\)".
accessibility.impact: Dragging the folder is the instruction on screen, and real folders are usually called 'Family Photos' or 'Photos d'été'. The first useful moment fails, the error shows backslashes, and the window has to be reopened.
accessibility.fix: In go.py: if a backslash is present use shlex.split(typed)[0], strip whitespace, and loop until the folder exists (or offer osascript 'choose folder'). In bash: VOL=$(printf '%s' "$VOL" | sed -E 's/\\(.)/\1/g').
accessibility.evidence: REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: go.ask_folder() with throwaway HOME and input patched to what Terminal inserts on a drag. '$D/f4/Family\ Photos ' gives '✗ There's nothing at $D/f4/Family\ Photos.' then exit code 1. "Photos\ d\'été " and 'Kandahar\ \(2011\) ' give the same, exit 1. Quoted or plain paths are accepted. Cause: go.py:101 only strips quotes and whitespace, and go.py:105-107 calls sys.exit(1). The make-drive launcher is partly better than claimed: it un-escapes '\ ' (line 47), so 'My\ Passport ' works. "Laszlo\'s\ Passport\ \(2TB\)" gives 'Nothing at …\'s Passport \(2TB\) — try again.' and it asks again rather than exiting; typing the list number then works. So the real defect is in go.py (Show me my life), which exits on any dragged folder with a space. Medium: it blocks the first run but nothing is harmed, and pressing return for ~/Pictures still works.

accessibility.title: 'What left the house' and the door switch depend on whether the drive is plugged in at that moment
accessibility.repro: $D/h_split.py: a Claude session with the drive unplugged writes 3 sends to ~/.jefferey/egress.jsonl. With the drive in, the report says 'Nothing. No send has been made…'. A door-shut file on the drive is not seen once the drive is unplugged.
accessibility.impact: The owner's only transparency tool reports no sends when his health appointment and his daughter's city were sent the day before. 'Unplug the drive and everything stops' is not true for JEFFEREY in Claude Desktop, which keeps running from the Mac with the door open.
accessibility.fix: Report from both the drive log and the Mac log, saying where each entry lives. is_shut() should be true if a shut file exists in either place. When the MCP or HTTP surface starts without the drive, say so in-band (in a tool result), not only on stderr.
accessibility.evidence: REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: Throwaway HOME, JEFFEREY_EGRESS/DOOR/CONSCIENCE unset (as install.py:152-160 writes the config; there is no SELFCLOUD_ROOT). 1) MCP session with no drive: root=None, log at ~/.jefferey/egress.jsonl. get_directives, get_conscience and what_left_the_house were all sent (3 lines). 2) egress.py report with SELFCLOUD_ROOT=$D/f5/drive: 'Nothing. No send has been made through the door in this period.' 3) shut with the drive in: 'The door is SHUT. Nothing leaves JEFFEREY until you open it.' (written to the drive). 4) Drive unplugged, new session: all 3 tools sent again. 5) Report with the drive back in: 'door is SHUT … Nothing.' while ~/.jefferey/egress.jsonl holds 6 sends. Cause: home._pick (home.py:113-136) moves every path, including the door switch (egress.py:312-317), to wherever the drive is. root() is decided once per process (home.py:65-90). This contradicts START_HERE.md:209: 'You want everything to stop → unplug the drive. That is the whole security model.'

accessibility.title: The egress report isn't in plain English, and its default action traps the person in less
accessibility.files: connector/egress.py:296-310, 659-700; connector/jefferey_mcp.py:94; What left the house.command:38
accessibility.repro: Run the launcher: '→ the engine JEFFEREY is riding (via mcp, key 'jefferey')', UTC 'Z' timestamps, 'tool_result', 'asked: []', raw JSON. Pressing Return opens less, and three more Returns don't leave it.
accessibility.impact: The default install never tells the owner his data went to Anthropic. Times are off by 4-5 hours. An older user stuck in a pager will close the window or give up.
accessibility.fix: Bind the MCP surface with engine 'Anthropic (Claude Desktop)'; HTTP tokens can carry a vendor label. Print local times in words, use plain names for tools ('your facts', 'your life story'), and summarise bodies. Drop less, or use less -FX with a printed 'press q to finish', or write the report to a .txt and `open` it in TextEdit.

accessibility.title: The wall isn't usable by touch, low vision or screen readers, and is English-only
accessibility.repro: In Chromium, iPad emulation shows only 🎤 and 'On this day', and the page says 'Press Escape'. lang is null, 0 of 3 images have alt, no aria-live region, the mic is named '🎤'. Captions are 16px on a 4K TV and 13px on a phone. At 320px the page scrolls sideways (430 vs 320). fr-CA shows French dates and English everywhere else.
accessibility.impact: These are the target users: people with dementia, low vision or no keyboard at a TV or tablet. Captions can't be read from the sofa, the privacy veil can't be reached when a visitor arrives, and VoiceOver users hear an unlabelled grid. Contrast is fine (5.4-5.8:1).
accessibility.fix: Add a large always-visible 'Hide' button. Scale captions with the viewport (e.g. clamp(16px,2.2vw,32px)) and add a text-size control. Set <html lang>, alt='Photo, 12 October 2019, Varadero, Cuba', aria-label on the input and mic, and role=status aria-live=polite on #reading. Use flex-wrap on the header. Put strings in a table with fr-CA.

accessibility.title: The wall passcode changes every start, there's no QR code, and the lockout blocks the correct link with the same message
accessibility.repro: 6 requests with yesterday's code return 403; today's correct code then also returns 403 'This screen needs the passcode shown in the terminal…' until restart. No QR is generated anywhere.
accessibility.impact: The kitchen tablet and TV, the surfaces for a person with dementia, stop working after every restart. The caregiver has to type a 22-character code with a remote, and after a few reloads the device is locked out with no explanation.
accessibility.fix: Keep a revocable per-device pairing token on the drive. Print a QR in Terminal and on the Mac's wall page. Time-box the lockout (e.g. a 60 s backoff) and give it its own message ('this screen used an old link — open the new one from the Mac'). Keep the 128-bit code.

accessibility.title: The wall misreads how older people and French speakers describe time and place
accessibility.repro: recall.parse: 'forty years ago', 'the 1980s', 'the seventies' and 'in the 80s' give no date. 'twenty-five years ago' gives 2021. 'Cuba il y a dix ans' returns all years, 'Noël' becomes 'no l', and 'Espagne' / 'juillet' are not understood.
accessibility.impact: Older users remember in decades and forty or fifty years back. The wall silently ignores those words, or picks the wrong year and states it with confidence. French speakers lose the date and place filters entirely.
accessibility.fix: Parse full number words up to 100, including hyphenated and spaced compounds (match compounds before single words). Treat decades as 10-year windows. Add French months, seasons, holidays and 'il y a N ans'. Add French place-name aliases (pycountry translations). Say in the reading line when part of the question wasn't understood.

accessibility.title: The album breaks in the situations it exists for: false dates, permanent 'no', unguarded first topic, lost stories
accessibility.repro: Scanned prints with EXIF but no date are asked about as 'from somewhere · October 2026'. 'no' declines a moment permanently with no undo. Ctrl-C or Ctrl-D gives a traceback and nothing is kept. A blank line ends the story and the next paragraph becomes the 'people'. The first question to the veteran is about Afghanistan.
accessibility.impact: These break the album's own rule ('states only facts'). The real photos of an elder's past never get dated. A confused 'no' loses a memory for good, a trauma topic opens the album, and a slow typist's words are lost or mangled.
accessibility.fix: Never use the file time as taken_at; show 'date unknown'. Let the caregiver date a batch of photos. Exclude the current year from 'On this day'. Make decline mean 'not now' unless confirmed, and let the owner undo it. Add an owner-set ask-first list of topics and places. In the CLI, save a draft on Ctrl-C or EOF and end with 'done' rather than a blank line. Add a 'Tell my stories.command' and a wall route that shows a moment's photos by ID.

accessibility.title: Access refusals on Claude Desktop reach the model as 'Error executing tool X'
accessibility.repro: JEFFEREY_CLIENT=claude-raw; call_tool('who_am_i') leads the SDK to return 'Error executing tool who_am_i', with the AccessDenied reason only in __cause__. The HTTP family key gets scope jargon.
accessibility.impact: An elder or family member hears 'there was an error' and retries, or gets talked through a workaround, instead of 'your Claude isn't allowed to see that'.
accessibility.fix: In the MCP door wrapper, catch AccessDenied and OwnerOnly and return {refused, reason, tell_the_user} in plain words without scope names. Pin the mcp version.

accessibility.title: Start-up collisions give tracebacks or 'set an environment variable'
accessibility.repro: wall.serve() on a port already held raises 'OSError: [Errno 98] Address already in use' (go.py has no try). With two marked drives: 'Say which with SELFCLOUD_ROOT=/Volumes/… Using neither.' on stderr, and the conscience falls back to ~/.jefferey.
accessibility.impact: Double-clicking twice crashes. A second (backup) drive silently sends the life to the Mac, and Claude Desktop users never see why.
accessibility.fix: Catch OSError: 'The wall is already open in another window.' For two drives, have the launchers list them and ask; on MCP or HTTP, return the problem as a result; never fall back silently.

accessibility.title: The 'no Terminal' promise doesn't hold at key steps
accessibility.repro: A new drive's Start launcher prints git clone and git checkout commands. Vault storage and self-test triage are typed Terminal commands. Changing the photo folder means deleting a hidden file. Instructions are printed in dim text.
accessibility.impact: Elderly buyers and families can't finish setup or recover alone, and the sensitive step (storing a secret) is the hardest one.
accessibility.fix: Ship a zip or .dmg (no git) and have 'Make this drive' copy the app onto the drive. Add a 'Keep a secret safe.command' using osascript dialogs, a 'Something went wrong.command' that saves the self-test output to the Desktop, and a 'Change my photo folder' question. Don't use dim text for instructions.

accessibility.title: Default ~/Pictures reads inside the Apple Photos library
accessibility.repro: photo_index.walk(~/Pictures) returns the original plus two derivatives inside 'Photos Library.photoslibrary'
accessibility.impact: Pressing Return, the easiest choice, fills the wall with duplicates and derivative copies. With iCloud's optimised storage, mostly derivatives are on the Mac at all.
accessibility.fix: Skip *.photoslibrary packages and say why, or read only originals/ with a warning about iCloud optimised storage. Point people to export or library/ instead.

accessibility.title: Terminal chat speaks to the AI instead of the person, and refuses harmless words
accessibility.repro: $D/h_chat.py: the refusal reads '…Tell the owner plainly; do not ask them to read it to you…'. 'the spare safety pin is in the sewing box' is refused as a PIN. With the door shut, the local engine refuses with no reopen hint. Nothing shows while the model thinks. 'bye' doesn't quit.
accessibility.impact: Confusing or alarming messages for older users, and no sign the program is working.
accessibility.fix: Separate text for the owner from guidance for the model. Require a digit or token after 'pin is'. When the door is shut on the local engine, say how to reopen it. Show 'thinking…'. Accept bye, goodbye and au revoir.

accessibility.title: Voice enrolment: English only, and a blank name becomes the account name
accessibility.repro: Pressing Return at 'Your name:' gives the consent sentence 'I am root.' The consent sentence and all 50 phrases are English.
accessibility.impact: A francophone's voice is captured reading a second language, and the consent recording names a computer account instead of the person.
accessibility.fix: Offer a French phrase sheet and consent sentence. Ask the name again rather than defaulting to id -un.

adversarial.title: Any client can revoke or narrow ANY key — a guest can brick the caretaker and tear down the inheritance keys
adversarial.repro: HTTP: with JEFFEREY_HTTP_TOKENS set, `curl -XDELETE '/selfcloud/grants?client=jefferey' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <gpt-raw token>'` returns 200 revoked:true; the owner's own Jefferey then loads 0 scopes and every data tool is denied. MCP: the default claude-raw session calling selfcloud_revoke('jefferey') does the same (g_mcp2.py: jefferey active True->False).
adversarial.impact: 'Deny by default' and 'revocation needs no permission because giving up authority is free' are conflated: the code lets client X give up client Y's authority. A compromised Custom GPT, a prompt-injected plain Claude Desktop session, or anyone who gets one bearer token can instantly disable the caretaker (the whole product stops working for the owner and the elderly/dementia users who depend on it), revoke the executor key (breaking digital inheritance), or quietly strip scopes from family. It is sabotage dressed up as 'narrowing'.
adversarial.files: connector/access.py:105-106 (OWNER_ONLY_TOOLS lists only widening); connector/selfcloud.py:146-165 (revoke/remove_scope); connector/jefferey_mcp.py:591,597 and connector/jefferey_http.py:706-715 (selfcloud_remove_scope/selfcloud_revoke carry neither @gate nor @owner_only)
adversarial.fix: Treat 'narrowing someone else's key' as a privileged act: make selfcloud_revoke and selfcloud_remove_scope @owner_only (console-only), OR allow a client to narrow/revoke only ITS OWN bound identity (current_client()==target) and require the owner console for any other target. A guest giving up its own key stays free; a guest killing the caretaker does not.
adversarial.evidence:
REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: Reproduced from scratch (fresh D, HOME, tokens jefferey:tokA,gpt-raw:tokB,family:tokC,executor:tokD, TestClient):
4 gpt-raw DELETE /selfcloud/grants?client=jefferey: 200 {"revoked": true, "client": "jefferey"}
5 jefferey GET /conscience: 403 "key revoked ..."
7 family POST /selfcloud/scopes/remove {executor, legacy.read}: 200 scopes []
8 executor GET /life: 403 "holds no key to this person's life layer"
9 control: gpt-raw POST /selfcloud/grants: 403 owner-only (widening is guarded, narrowing others is not).
MCP: default claude-raw process selfcloud_revoke('jefferey') -> revoked:true; next JEFFEREY_CLIENT=jefferey process get_conscience -> error; owner terminal also refused until owner re-runs selfcloud_grant from console (recovery exists). Extra: the access log records {client:'jefferey', action:'revoke'} — the TARGET, not the actor; only the egress log shows to='gpt-raw'. This is intended code (access.py:18-21, 103-106 'Narrowing never needs the owner's console'; selfcloud.py:146-165; jefferey_mcp.py:590-600; jefferey_http.py:706-715 have no gate), so RISK not FAIL: the design lets client X strip client Y.

adversarial.title: Destructive conscience tools mass-delete the whole life on an empty/wildcard argument, with no guard
adversarial.repro: As the caretaker key (owner terminal / Claude Desktop): dispatch_tool('forget',{'contains':''}) -> removes every fact; forget_life('') -> wipes all memories+media+people; remove_rule('') -> deletes all rules; close_goal('')/conscience_exclude('') likewise (g_owner.py output).
adversarial.impact: The life layer and legacy archive are the irreplaceable core of the product (a veteran's Afghanistan photos, a dying person's stories for their family). A single tool call with an empty string erases all of it, and any prompt injection the model obeys at a writer surface triggers it. There is no confirmation, no cap, no 'are you sure'. This is latent data loss of exactly what cannot be recovered.
adversarial.files: connector/conscience.py:371-377 (forget_fact: ''.lower() in every fact), 462-469 (close_goal); connector/life.py:125-140 (forget_life); connector/rules.py:117-126 (remove_rule), 75-83 (exclude)
adversarial.fix: Reject empty/whitespace-only match strings in every bulk-delete path (return a no-op with a clear message). For deletions above a small count, require an explicit confirmation token or route through an owner-console-only bulk operation. The history snapshots already exist — surface a one-step undo.
adversarial.evidence:
REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: Terminal, JEFFEREY_CLIENT=jefferey, fresh store seeded with 3 facts, 2 goals, 1 person/memory/media, 1 rule, 1 inclusion:
BEFORE {facts:3, goals_active:2, memories:1, media:1, people:1, rules:1, included:1}
forget {'contains': ''} -> removed_facts 3; close_goal '' -> closed 2; forget_life '' -> memories 1, media 1, people 1; remove_rule '' -> removed 1; conscience_exclude '' -> excluded 1
AFTER all zero.
MCP caretaker (Claude Desktop, JEFFEREY_CLIENT=jefferey): forget {'contains':' '} -> removed_facts 2 (a single space also matches everything; forget_fact does not strip).
Worse than reported: recovery window collapses. Right after the wipe 11 of 20 history snapshots still held facts; after 12 harmless list_rules calls: 0 of 20 — every gate check writes the access log (selfcloud.py:206-211 -> _save -> _archive, HISTORY_KEEP=20 conscience.py:37,319). Code: conscience.py:371-377, 462-469; life.py:125-140; rules.py:75-83, 117-126 (''/whitespace is a substring of every string). No restore tool exists on any surface.

adversarial.title: The egress secret-scan is trivially evaded by separators and misses whole secret classes — secrets both leave and enter
adversarial.repro: Out: egress.release_text('you_said','4111.1111.1111.1111') returns LEFT (dotted), as do newline-split cards, 'my password hunter2xx', 'my pin 4821', bank account numbers and IBANs (g_egress.py). In: dispatch_tool('remember_fact',{'fact':'card 4111.1111.1111.1111'}) is admitted and stored, and explain_basis('card') then returns it verbatim to the engine.
adversarial.impact: The product's headline promise is 'secrets never enter model context; nothing leaves unscanned.' A card the owner is socially-engineered into typing with dots, or a secret an engine hands in with dots, defeats the scan outright — the card is sent to Anthropic/OpenAI, or stored and re-exported on the next read. Bank/IBAN numbers have no pattern at all even though representative.py already treats them as sensitive on forms. This is a direct secret/PII leak off the owner's machine.
adversarial.files: connector/egress.py:216 (_CARD only allows single space/hyphen between digits), 219-220 (_PASSWORD requires is/:/= delimiter), 226-244 (looks_secret: no bank/routing/IBAN patterns)
adversarial.fix: Before Luhn, strip all non-digits across a sliding window so any separator (dot, newline, NBSP) is caught; broaden the password/PIN heuristic (any high-entropy token near the words, or any labelled-secret); add account/routing/IBAN patterns. Keep the field allowlist as the primary control and treat the scan as defense-in-depth, not the sole barrier.
adversarial.evidence:
REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: Fresh process, egress.release_text('you_said', s) on the chat surface:
refused 'card 4111 1111 1111 1111' (control)
LEFT 'card 4111.1111.1111.1111', '4111\n1111\n1111\n1111', '4111  1111  1111  1111' (double space), '4111/1111/...', NBSP-separated
LEFT 'my password hunter2xx', 'my pin 4821' (refused only with is/:/=)
LEFT 'SIN 046.454.286', 'SSN 078 05 1120', 'IBAN GB82 WEST 1234 5698 7654 32', 'transit 00123 inst 004 acct 1234567', 'sk-ant-api03 abcdefghijklmnop'
Inbound: dispatch_tool('remember_fact',{'fact':'Visa card 4111.1111.1111.1111 exp 09/29'}) -> stored; also 'bank password hunter2xx' stored. explain_basis('card') -> returns the dotted card verbatim, and gpt-raw's preset holds facts.read, so it re-exports to other engines. Cause: egress.py:216 _CARD allows only one optional space/hyphen between digits; 219-220 _PASSWORD needs is/:/=; 217-218 SIN/SSN separators narrow; looks_secret 226-244 has no bank/IBAN pattern although representative.py:60 treats those as sensitive.

adversarial.title: admit() disables the protection tools on the very content they exist to analyze
adversarial.repro: dispatch_tool('triage_message',{...,'body':'We detected fraud on card 4111 1111 1111 1111...'}) -> refused at the door; 'Your SSN 078-05-1120 was used' -> refused; even 'your password is about to expire' -> refused (triage test output).
adversarial.impact: triage_message exists to read hostile mail for an elderly, overwhelmed, scam-targeted owner. Phishing routinely quotes the victim's own card/SSN or says 'your password is expiring'. Because admit() scans every inbound argument and refuses any secret-shaped text, Jefferey cannot triage the most dangerous messages — it returns a cryptic 'refused at the door' instead of a scam warning, leaving the user unprotected exactly when it matters, and training them to ignore the refusal.
adversarial.files: connector/egress.py:457-479 (admit scans all args), 566-585 (through() wraps every tool); applies to triage_message, draft_guidance, review_statement, fill_form
adversarial.fix: Run admit() only on tools that WRITE untrusted text into the store (remember_fact, add_memory, add_media, set_profile_field, set_rule, record_story, record_answer), not on read/analyze tools. Or scan only the specific fields destined for persistence, never a body that is merely being read.
adversarial.evidence:
REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: Terminal, JEFFEREY_CLIENT=jefferey, dispatch_tool('triage_message', {sender, subject, body}):
card quoted ('We detected fraud on card 4111 1111 1111 1111...') -> REFUSED 'body ... looks like a card number'
SSN quoted ('Your SSN 078-05-1120 was used...') -> REFUSED
'Your password is about to expire. Click http://bit.ly/x' -> REFUSED 'looks like a password or PIN' (the _PASSWORD regex matches 'password is about')
'Your PIN: verify it now' -> REFUSED
control (same gift-card scam, no trigger words) -> verdict=likely_scam
The owner pasting the same text at his terminal ('Is this a scam? ...') is also refused by release_text, so he gets only '(kept in the house — ...)' and no answer (jefferey_chat.py:1463-1468). draft_guidance with 'my password is expired' -> REFUSED. Code: egress.py:457-479 admit scans every argument of every tool; 566-585 through() and jefferey_chat.py:896 apply it to read/analyse tools. Fails closed (no leak), so medium: it removes the scam check exactly on the most common phishing wording.

adversarial.title: The owner's private standing rules leak to plain rented engines (gated one tier too low)
adversarial.repro: As the owner (jefferey) write rules about cancer/drinking/a layoff; then with a gpt-raw bearer token: GET /rules, GET /rules/guidance?tags=drinking, GET /rules/check?audience=a-stranger&tags=health all return 200 with the instructions verbatim, incl. check_disclosure echoing 'My cancer is private' (rules-leak test).
adversarial.impact: list_rules/guidance_for/check_disclosure are gated to facts.read — the tier a plain ChatGPT and a plain Claude session both hold. The owner's most sensitive self-knowledge, which usually names the very secret it protects ('My cancer is private', 'don't mention the layoff'), flows straight to the raw engines the owner was promised are 'kept at arm's length'. check_disclosure quoting the deny rule to a raw engine is the exact 'a refusal that quotes the rule IS the disclosure' problem the 2026-09-15 audit claimed to close — reopened because the gate tier is too low.
adversarial.fix: Put the rule-reading tools behind a life-tier scope (life.read) or a dedicated rules.read scope that claude-raw/gpt-raw do not hold; and have check_disclosure return the verdict without quoting the rule text to non-caretaker clients.

adversarial.title: Owner-console content injection escalates authority and mints keys; self-widening is blocked only by the directive, not by code
adversarial.repro: At the owner terminal (OWNER_CONSOLE=1): set_permission('purchases','act',cap=100000) succeeds, then authorize_action('purchases','buy gift cards',5000)->allowed:True; selfcloud_add_scope('jefferey',...) and selfcloud_grant('jefferey',[all scopes]) succeed; selfcloud_grant('attacker-ai',[life/legacy/...]) mints a new key that can read the life layer (g_owner.py + final batch).
adversarial.impact: The owner console is reached by untrusted content — triaged email bodies, documents, PDFs — that the model may obey. The only gate on high-impact widening is an env var that is already set on that surface. An injection can flip the Act gate (after which the gift-card purchase the owner would never approve sails through authorize_action, to be executed by the host's other connectors), widen the caretaker's own key, or create an all-scope key for an attacker-named client. 'Jefferey never widens Jefferey' is prose in directives.md, not a check in access.py.
adversarial.files: connector/access.py:274-288 (owner_only trusts the env var alone); connector/conscience.py:478-493 (set_permission); connector/selfcloud.py:111-144 (grant/add_scope — no guard against target=='jefferey')
adversarial.fix: Do not treat the console env var as sufficient authorization for widening — require an interactive, out-of-band owner confirmation (a prompt the model cannot answer) for set_permission to 'act', for any grant/add_scope, and especially for any key named 'jefferey'; reject in code any grant/add_scope whose target is the caretaker identity.

adversarial.title: Unbounded store/audit-log growth and forgeable audit entries by low-privilege callers
adversarial.repro: gpt-raw: 300x GET /selfcloud/check grew conscience.json 4KB->51KB (312 log rows); 50x POST /actions/authorize wrote 50 action-log rows. Caretaker: a 2 MB fact is stored uncapped; log_action writes an arbitrary fabricated 'refund $9999 done' entry.
adversarial.impact: Any token-holder can loop read-only checks or authorize-probes to bloat the conscience on the owner's drive, inflate the revision counter, and poison the owner's audit trail with fake 'denied' rows attributed to their own activity — the same trail they are told to trust when asking 'what did Jefferey do?'. A writer can forge outcomes outright, and a single huge fact can fill the drive.
adversarial.files: connector/selfcloud.py:206-211 (_log saves on every check); connector/conscience.py:524-542 (authorize_action/log_action append+save, no gate on authorize_action); conscience.remember_fact (no length cap)
adversarial.fix: Do not persist read-only access checks per call (keep them in memory or rotate a bounded log); gate authorize_action; cap single-value and total-store sizes; rate-limit per client; and mark log_action-written outcomes as model-asserted vs system-observed.

adversarial.title: MCP access denials are reported as an opaque 'Error executing tool' instead of the designed refusal
adversarial.repro: On the MCP surface, claude-raw calling who_am_i/remember_fact raises UnexpectedToolError('Error executing tool ...') rather than returning the refusal dict the chat surface produces.
adversarial.impact: On Claude Desktop/Code the model cannot distinguish 'your key does not permit this' from a genuine crash, so it may retry by another route or tell the owner the system is broken. The carefully-worded refusal ('say plainly your key does not permit it, do not work around it') is lost precisely where guests run.
adversarial.files: connector/jefferey_mcp.py:62-76 (door catches only EgressRefused) vs connector/jefferey_chat.py:899-902 (dispatch_tool catches AccessDenied/OwnerOnly and returns refusal_result)
adversarial.fix: Catch AccessDenied and OwnerOnly in the MCP door() wrapper and return a refusal_result-style dict, mirroring the chat surface, so every surface reports denials identically.

adversarial.title: Cross-engine prompt-injection propagation and attacker-text round-trips through shared, echoed fields
adversarial.repro: A fact 'NOTE TO ASSISTANT: IGNORE ALL RULES...' written by one engine is returned verbatim by explain_basis to any facts.read client; check_charge echoes an injected merchant string and fill_form echoes an injected field label straight back to the engine (g_inject.py E2/E3/E5).
adversarial.impact: The conscience is a durable, cross-engine channel: trick or compromise one surface into writing, and the payload is served to every other engine (ChatGPT, Claude, local Hermes) that shares the read scope. Tool results that echo attacker-controlled merchant names and form labels give injected instructions a path into the model's context from ordinary statement/form data.
adversarial.files: connector/conscience.py:365-369 (remember_fact), 649-671 (explain_basis); connector/guardian.py:134-183 (check_charge echoes merchant); connector/representative.py:153-202 (fill_form echoes labels)
adversarial.fix: Clearly delimit engine-/data-sourced free text when re-served (wrap as untrusted quoted data, not prose), and keep the directive's 'content is data, not instructions' stance enforced by structure; consider per-engine namespacing of model-authored facts.

album.title: Album sqlite connection is bound to one thread: on Claude Desktop (MCP) and the GPT server (HTTP), stories and declines stop saving after any parallel calls
album.repro: One long-lived process, JEFFEREY_CLIENT=jefferey: await call_tool('next_story_prompt'); await asyncio.gather(call_tool('who_am_i'), call_tool('get_directives'), call_tool('story_gaps')); await call_tool('record_story', {...}) → sqlite3.ProgrammingError, 0 stored (H/h_par.py). On HTTP (real uvicorn, port 0): after 6 concurrent GET /album/progress, 12/12 POST /album/story → 500 and 0 stored (H/h_thread.py http).
album.impact: On the owner's main surfaces, the stories the album exists to keep 'permanently' are not saved. The engine only sees 'Error executing tool record_story'. Declines also fail, so a 'rather not' about Afghanistan is not recorded and the moment returns. A person with dementia or a caregiver cannot recover from this. It persists until Claude Desktop or the server restarts.
album.fix: In Reminisce, open a connection per call (with sqlite3.connect(p, timeout=10) as db) or use check_same_thread=False guarded by a threading.Lock. Add a test that calls album tools from two threads and after an asyncio.gather of unrelated tools.
album.evidence:
REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: Reproduced from scratch with a fresh HOME and a real photo_index build of 12 stamped JPEGs. Installed mcp is 2.3.0, which runs sync tools through anyio.to_thread (mcpserver/utilities/func_metadata.py:164). reminisce.py:110 opens one connection with sqlite3.connect(p) and reuses it from whichever worker thread runs the next call.
MCP, JEFFEREY_CLIENT=jefferey: next_story_prompt, then 6 rounds of [asyncio.gather(who_am_i, get_directives, story_gaps); record_story]. Result: 'UnexpectedToolError: Error executing tool record_story' in 4 of 6 rounds, so 2 of 6 memories stored. The root cause of the exception is 'ProgrammingError SQLite objects created in a thread can only be used in that same thread'. decline_story fails the same way (3 of 4 rounds). With no gather, 5 of 5 calls succeed. On MCP the failure is intermittent rather than total.
HTTP, real uvicorn on port 0: GET /album/next returns 200. Then 6 parallel GET /album/progress give [200,500,500,500,500,500]. Then 12 sequential POST /album/story give 12 x 500, and 0 memories are stored. stderr shows the same ProgrammingError 17 times. Severity: the story the owner told is never written, and on HTTP this lasts until the server restarts. || IMPACT CONFIRMED: Could not refute it. On MCP it is worse than reported: no parallel calls are needed. reminisce.py:102-110 opens one cached sqlite3.connect() lazily, in whichever thread calls it first. mcp 2.3.0 (requirements.txt has an unpinned mcp[cli]; install.py:126 upgrades) runs sync tools through anyio.to_thread (func_metadata.py:164). The stdio transport reads…

album.title: 'Rather not' is not durable: declines are keyed to an index file and a cluster start date, and cover one 14-day cluster rather than the subject
album.repro: Decline afghanistan-20111003, then add one Kabul photo dated 2011-10-01 and rebuild → 'afghanistan-20111001' (9 photos) offered (album-06). Build a fresh index of the same photos → the declined id is offered again (album-07). Unplug the drive → the laptop index offers Afghanistan again, with 0 stories visible (album-20). After declining Kabul 2011, Kandahar 2012 is offered 3 prompts later (album-05).
album.impact: A veteran who said 'rather not' about his Afghanistan photos is asked about them again through ordinary events: an iCloud sync, a re-index, moving the index to the drive, or unplugging the drive. This is the exact harm the rule exists to prevent, for him and for people with dementia.
album.fix: Keep album state (declined/told, plus the sha set) in the conscience, which travels with the person. Treat any cluster that shares a photo sha with a declined moment as declined. Offer place/country/tag-level 'never ask about X' that the album honours. When the drive's index is absent, say so instead of falling back to another index.
album.evidence:
REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: Reproduced from scratch with a real photo_index build.
(a) The id is keyed to the cluster's first date (reminisce.py:159, mid=f"{slug}-{start}"). Steps: decline afghanistan-20111003 (4 Kabul photos). Then add one Kabul photo dated 2011-10-01 and rebuild the index incrementally. next_prompt now offers afghanistan-20111001: 'There are 5 photographs from Afghanistan (Kabul) · October 2011. Tell me about that'. The table holds both rows: afghanistan-20111001 untold (5 photos) and afghanistan-20111003 declined (4 photos). The new moment contains the declined photos.
(b) Decline state lives only in index.sqlite (reminisce.py:111-122). Declining in one index and then building a fresh index of the same photos gives 'fresh index offers hungary-20190210', the declined id. The conscience holds no album state at all (no moment, album or decline keys).
Not a defect: Kandahar 2012 being offered after Kabul 2011 matches the documented per-moment design (reminisce.py:26). The unplugged-drive case also moves the conscience (home.py:113-118), so it only matters if an old laptop index exists. The core claim, that the decline is undone by ordinary sync or re-indexing, is confirmed.

album.title: The album ignores the owner's own rules, his people, the intake gate and earned trust
album.repro: Write the reaction rule 'Never bring up Afghanistan unless I raise it first' (tags afghanistan,war,kabul), conscience_exclude('afghanistan'), 'Don't bring up Mum's funeral', and add_person Ilona 'died February 2019'. Then next_prompt() ×3 → Kabul, then Budapest Feb 2019, then Cuba (album-15/16). With trust 0 the first ask is the war (album-02).
album.impact: The owner's explicit instructions about trauma and grief are bypassed by the feature most likely to trigger them. The rules engine promises enforcement, not etiquette, and the album skips it.
album.fix: Before offering, call rules.guidance_for(tags=[country, place]) and skip moments with any matching reaction rule or exclusion. Require interview trust ≥2 before the album opens. Prefer small, recent, non-flagged moments first. Let the owner mark places as sensitive. Make follow-ups trauma-aware: no 'how does it feel now' for flagged topics.
album.evidence:
REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: Executed with a fresh conscience and index. set_rule('reaction','afghanistan,war,kabul','Never bring up Afghanistan unless I raise it first.') and a rule 'Don't bring up Mum's funeral' tagged budapest/ilona. add_person Ilona: 'died February 2019, funeral in Budapest'. Interview trust is score 1, max_depth 1.
next_prompt() three times returned hungary-20190210 all three times: 'There are 5 photographs from Hungary (Budapest) · February 2019. Tell me about that'. After that moment is told, the next offer is afghanistan-20111003: 'There are 4 photographs from Afghanistan (Kabul)…'. Meanwhile guidance_for('afghanistan') returns the rule verbatim.
The prompt's keys are ask, from, label, moment_id, photo_ids, photos, rule, show_on_the_wall and to. None of them points the engine to guidance_for. next_prompt (reminisce.py:184-219) never reads the rules, the people or interview trust. It always returns the same largest untold moment, so an engine that obeys the rule can only skip the album forever, or decline on the owner's behalf.
Why RISK rather than FAIL: directives.md:218 does tell the engine to call guidance_for before sensitive subjects, so the protection rests on the engine. The intake-gate part is weak: exclude() only edits the conscience_included list, and the album is an owner-requested feature.

album.title: Photo sha256 hashes trip the egress secret scan (SIN/card), so one pinned photo blacks out the life layer for every engine
album.repro: 48 of 3000 real JPEG hashes (1.6%) make egress.looks_secret() fire. Build a 4-photo Varadero trip with one such photo: next_story_prompt is refused; record_story stores the story but returns 'withheld… looks like a social insurance number'; who_am_i and tell_story are then refused permanently (H/h8_luhn.py).
album.impact: About 18% of 12-photo prompts are refused. After a handful of stories, who_am_i and tell_story fail on Claude, GPT and Hermes, and for family and executor too if the story is shared. The engine tells an elderly owner his anniversary story 'contains a social insurance number'. The engine believes the story wasn't kept and retries, creating duplicates.
album.fix: Don't hand raw hashes to engines: use short opaque ids such as moment index numbers, or strip the photos and photo_ids lists from released results and keep them home. At minimum, require non-alphanumeric boundaries in the _CARD and _SIN regexes so digit runs inside hex are not matched.
album.evidence:
REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: Executed. 3000 real stamped JPEGs: 56 of their sha256 values (1.87%) trip egress.looks_secret() (45 as a SIN, 11 as a card number). 20000 random hex hashes: 1.645%. The _SIN and _CARD lookarounds (egress.py:216-217) only exclude neighbouring digits, so letters a-f count as boundaries.
MCP test (JEFFEREY_CLIENT=jefferey): a 4-photo Varadero trip including the photo with sha 1fce302217229d94…, whose digits 302217229 pass Luhn.
- next_story_prompt: refused, "'photo_ids[3]' contains what looks like a social insurance number".
- record_story: refused, "'memory.photos[3]'…". The memory is nevertheless stored (memories stored: 1), so the engine is told it failed when it did not.
- who_am_i and tell_story: refused, "'moments[0].photos[3]' contains what looks like a social insurance number". This persists for every later call.
- story_progress: still works.
At about 1.7% per hash, a 143-photo moment has roughly a 90% chance of containing a tripping hash. Severity is high, not critical: nothing leaves the house, but the core life-layer reads go dark and the engine is misled.

album.title: Shutting the door does not stop writes: record, decline and erase all execute while 'offline'
album.repro: Create JEFFEREY_DOOR, then MCP forget_life({'contains':'14th'}) → memories 1→0, while the result says 'withheld… Nothing from this result left the house' (album-40). decline_story leaves status 'declined' and record_story stores a memory, both reported as refused (album-41).
album.impact: The owner's off switch doesn't stop a misbehaving or compromised engine from erasing or declining his stories. The engine is told nothing happened, so it retries or reports wrongly.
album.fix: Check egress.is_shut() in admit(), before the tool function runs, for every tool. Refuse with 'the door is shut; nothing was done'.
album.evidence:
REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: Executed over MCP (JEFFEREY_CLIENT=jefferey). Kept one story mentioning 'the 14th', then created the JEFFEREY_DOOR file; egress.is_shut() returned True.
- forget_life({'contains':'14th'}) returned {'refused': true, 'reason': 'withheld by the egress door: the owner has shut the door (JEFFEREY is offline). Nothing from this result left t…'}, yet memories went from 1 to 0.
- decline_story(afghanistan-20111003) was refused, yet the table shows ('afghanistan-20111003','declined').
- record_story('planted while offline') was refused, yet the memory is stored.
The egress log records each of these only as 'refused=the owner has shut the door', so 'What left the house' also hides that the write happened.
Cause: egress.through() (egress.py:575-578) runs admit() and then the tool function, and only release() checks is_shut() (egress.py:490). admit() (egress.py:457) never checks it.

album.title: 'Verbatim' is unenforced and memories carry no provenance; the terminal claims 'kept his words' for a paraphrase
album.repro: A fake local Hermes (127.0.0.1:0) answers the owner's typed story with record_story(text='The user served in Kabul in 2011…'). The stored text is the paraphrase and the trace prints 'kept his words, pinned to 8 photos' (album-39). A compromised caretaker engine declines all 7 moments and plants a legacy 'confession'. Memory keys are only text, when, people, tags, visibility, added, photos (album-38, album-11).
album.impact: His words are replaced by an engine's summary or a fabrication, and later read back to him and his family as his own. With dementia, this is how false memories are made.
album.fix: Store source (surface, client, engine) and told_by on every memory. On the terminal, mark verbatim only when the normalised text appears in what the owner typed this session, otherwise store verbatim:false and say so. Make legacy writes and bulk declines need owner confirmation.
album.evidence:
REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: Executed run_turn_local against a fake OpenAI-compatible server on 127.0.0.1:0. The owner typed: 'I was in Kabul in October 2011. Mike drove the convoy, and the dust got into everything.' The fake model called next_story_prompt, then record_story(text='The user served in Kabul in 2011 and recalls dusty convoys.').
Terminal output: '· opening the album: Hungary (Budapest) · February 2019 (5 photos) | · kept his words, pinned to 5 photos | Jefferey Kept, in your words.'
Stored text: 'The user served in Kabul in 2011 and recalls dusty convoys.' It is a paraphrase, and it is pinned to the Budapest photos. Memory keys: added, people, photos, tags, text, visibility, when. There is no source, engine, surface or verbatim flag.
The 'kept his words' trace is unconditional on kept=True (jefferey_chat.py:1165-1167). reminisce.record and life.add_memory (life.py:79-100) store whatever text they are given. Verbatim is only a directive to the model. RISK because it needs a model that paraphrases, which is common for small local models.

album.title: Visibility is chosen by the engine and can't be changed later
album.repro: record_answer('health_watch', "Early Alzheimer's diagnosis in May. Don't tell the kids yet.", visibility='family') → the family ceiling reads it (album-49). record_story(…, visibility='family') for a convoy story → the family reads it (album-14). No set_visibility tool exists (grep across connector/).
album.impact: Private health and trauma reach family against his stated wish. Raising visibility is a widening act, yet it needs no owner confirmation, and he has no tool to lower it again without deleting the story.
album.fix: Store new stories and answers private, always. Widening (to family or legacy) only from the owner console or after explicit confirmation. Add set_visibility (narrowing free, widening owner-only).
album.evidence:
REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: Executed on HTTP (TestClient, jefferey token tokA, family token tokC).
POST /interview/answer {question_id:'call_first', answer:"Early Alzheimer's diagnosis in May. Don't tell the kids yet.", visibility:'family'} returned 200 recorded/answered. A family-token GET /life then returned moments: ["Early Alzheimer's diagnosis in May. Don't tell the kids yet."].
The visibility argument comes from the engine and is used as given (interview.py:223, reminisce.py:242, life.py:88). No owner confirmation is needed to widen it, while widening keys requires JEFFEREY_OWNER_CONSOLE. No set_visibility or change_visibility exists: grep across connector/ found nothing, and the OpenAPI spec has no visibility route. The only way to narrow an entry is forget_life plus re-adding it. RISK because it needs the engine to pick the wrong audience, but the result is private health information reaching family against the owner's stated wish.

album.title: Absent photos are still offered: unplugged sources aren't marked missing and stale moment rows are never re-checked
album.repro: Rename the source folder, scan_once → (0,0,0,0) and Kabul is offered with 0/8 reachable (album-18). Delete the files, scan_once marks 8 missing, Kabul is still offered (album-19). With no drive and no laptop index, the reply is 'No photographs are indexed yet' (album-20).
album.impact: 'There are 8 photographs…' while nothing can be shown on the wall. A person with dementia is asked about pictures nobody can find. Contradicts FOUNDER_DIRECTIONS §4½.
album.fix: In next_prompt, recount live photos (missing_since IS NULL and path reachable) and skip moments with none. scan_once should record 'source unreachable' state. Report 'your drive is out' rather than 'nothing indexed'.

album.title: Wrong or useless 'facts' in prompts: dead-clock dates, undated scans invisible, a whole life as one moment
album.repro: EXIF date 0000:00:00 in Kabul → 'There are 3 photographs from Afghanistan (Kabul) · October 2026' (album-23). Scans with no EXIF: taken_at NULL and never offered (album-21). Everyday Toronto photos merge into one 120-photo moment; with 80k (simulated) rows → 'There are 80120 photographs… Jan 2014–Nov 2025', pinned to 80,120 shas, conscience 6.09 MB (album-24).
album.impact: Breaks the rule that prompts state only facts: a false date reaches a confused person. The most important grief material, old prints, is never asked about. The biggest-first prompt is meaningless and bloats every save and snapshot.
album.fix: Record date_source and leave mtime-fallback dates out of the album (or say 'date unknown'). Add a tool to date or place a group of scans. Split home-country clusters by month or by being away from home, and cap pinned photos (store moment id plus a sample).

album.title: Erasure is incomplete and blunt
album.repro: Story 'We were up at Bagram…'; forget_life('Afghanistan') → 0 and forget_life('Kabul') → 0 (album-32). forget_life('a') → all 3 stories gone, no confirmation (album-31). After forget_life('convoy') the text remains twice in egress.jsonl and in 2 history snapshots; story_progress still counts it (album-30).
album.impact: A person who can't recall his exact words can't erase a story by its subject. One stray letter wipes everything. 'Erasable forever after' is not true while the egress log keeps every story verbatim.
