privacy.impact: People who never agreed are profiled. Their medical news is retained forever and sent to engine providers, and a child's school and medication sit in a log.
privacy.fix: Log triage as sender domain plus hash, not the body. Add a 'minor' and 'third-party sensitive' flag that defaults to private and is withheld from engines. Warn when 'family' visibility is chosen for someone else's health.

privacy.title: No route for an authorised representative and no legal paperwork
privacy.repro: family token: DELETE /facts and DELETE /life -> 403. No privacy policy, PIA or export tool in either repo.
privacy.impact: For a parent with dementia, the attorney or substitute decision-maker cannot access, correct or erase. A Quebec customer has no Law 25 s.17 assessment for data sent to US engines. Self-Cloud catalog erasure cannot be verified here.
privacy.fix: Add a 'representative' preset (read and erase with owner-set conditions, every act logged). Add a one-command export bundle (conscience, index rows, voice manifest, egress). Write a privacy policy and a PIA before anything is sold.

privacy.title: Public and onboarding claims overstate protection
privacy.repro: conscience.json is plaintext JSON (hA.py '42' True) while the site says 'encrypted'. 'Patent pending' after lapse. START_HERE.md:95-96 'nothing leaves the Mac by it'. ENCRYPT_THE_DRIVE.md:282 'A border officer sees noise'.
privacy.impact: Misleading privacy and IP claims to elderly buyers create Competition Act and privacy-regulator exposure. Owners make decisions (travel, consent) on false premises.
privacy.fix: Fix the site text now (MASTER_BUILD_LIST 1.6). Reword START_HERE to say results go to Anthropic. Add honest border guidance: compelled-passcode risk, ship the drive separately, no keychain auto-mount.

privacy.title: Metadata leaks and labelling errors
privacy.repro: gpt-raw GET /egress lists family and executor key use; family GET /selfcloud/log 200; claude-raw pdf_form_fields confirms tax-return.pdf exists; is_this_machine('http://127.evil.example') True; the access log grew by 76 entries in one session
privacy.impact: Engines and relatives learn who uses which key (an executor key in use implies death or incapacity) and which private documents exist. A non-loopback host can be logged as 'stays in the house'.
privacy.fix: Scope what_left_the_house to the caller's own sends. Gate selfcloud_status, grants and log to the owner. Gate pdf_form_fields and confine it to the drive. Use ipaddress.ip_address(host).is_loopback after resolving. Cap and roll up the access log.

scale.title: SQLite connections are shared across threads, so the wall and the album fail under normal use
scale.repro: Build any index, then in one process: import wall; srv=wall.serve(idx,0,lan=False); wall._index() (as wall.main() does); start serve_forever in a thread; GET /status → HTTP 500 'ProgrammingError: SQLite objects created in a thread can only be used in that same thread'. Without the main-thread call (the go.py path), fetching 6 thumbnails in parallel gives 36/36 500s. MCP: asyncio.gather of 12 next_story_prompt → 11 UnexpectedToolError<-ProgrammingError. HTTP: /album/next through the threadpool → 12–14 of 18 errors.
scale.impact: The wall, the product's photo screen for the family and the person with dementia, shows nothing when started as documented ('python tools/wall.py') and broken images when started from Show me my life. Opening the album from Claude or a GPT fails intermittently. The bundled selftests pass only because sequential threads reuse a thread id, which hides the bug.
scale.fix: Open a connection per request or per thread (threading.local), or connect with check_same_thread=False and guard it with a lock. Do the same in Reminisce.db. Add selftests that make parallel requests and that call _index() from the main thread before serving.
scale.evidence: REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: Fresh tmp dir/HOME, synthetic 3,000-photo index (60 real JPEGs). f0_wall.py: (a) the wall.main() path (serve, then _index() on the main thread, as tools/wall.py:358-359 does): /status 500, /on-this-day 500, 36/36 parallel thumbs 500, all 'ProgrammingError: SQLite objects created in a thread can only be used in that same thread'. (b) the go.py path (tools/go.py:169, no main-thread call): sequential /status 200 and /on-this-day 200 (60 hits), then 6-way parallel thumbs {500: 36}, parallel on-this-day {500: 18}. MCP with JEFFEREY_CLIENT=jefferey (mcp 2.3.0 runs sync tools through anyio.to_thread, func_metadata.py:164): gather of 12 next_story_prompt gives 1 ok and 11 UnexpectedToolError caused by ProgrammingError. In one long-lived loop, sequential calls are fine but 2 parallel calls give 1 ProgrammingError. HTTP TestClient /album/next: 4 sequential are 200, 18 parallel are {500: 17, 200: 1}. Cause: sqlite3.connect without check_same_thread (photo_index.py:85, reminisce.py:110).

scale.title: Photo content hashes trip the SIN/card scan, so album stories make who_am_i and tell_story permanently unreadable
scale.repro: In h/harness_i_hash.py: 1.66% of hashlib.sha256(os.urandom(32)).hexdigest() values match _SIN or _CARD with Luhn. With JEFFEREY_CLIENT=jefferey on a real 3,000-photo index: call_tool next_story_prompt → record_story(moment_id, text) → REFUSED ('memory.photos[208] ... card number'), yet the memory is stored; after that who_am_i and tell_story → REFUSED whole.
scale.impact: The more photos a story covers, the surer the poisoning: 50 ids give 57%, 200 give 96%. With 80k photos it is certain. After the veteran's first album story, no engine can read who he is or tell his story. That is the 'poisoned aggregate' admit() was written to prevent, arriving from the index instead. The engine is told nothing was kept although it was, which invites duplicate retries.
scale.fix: Exempt values that are exactly 64 hex characters (content ids) from the scan, or require non-hex boundaries ((?<![0-9a-fA-F]) and (?![0-9a-fA-F])) on the SIN and card patterns. Return a count and at most about 12 ids from record_story, and store a moment id plus a small sample instead of every hash. Leave photo id lists out of who_am_i and tell_story.
scale.evidence: REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: f01_mcp.py poison: egress.looks_secret flags 325 of 20,000 random sha256 hex strings (1.62%), because _SIN and _CARD (egress.py:217-218) only exclude neighbouring decimal digits, so a run of digits inside hex passes Luhn. With JEFFEREY_CLIENT=jefferey on MCP: next_story_prompt gives afghanistan-20110301 (2,940 photos). record_story gives {refused: true, reason: "'memory.photos[66]' contains what looks like a card number..."}, yet 1 memory was stored with 2,940 hashes pinned (reminisce.py:238-240, life.py:96-97), 42 of which trip the scan. After that, who_am_i and tell_story both return refused ('moments[0].photos[66] ... card number'). Adding an unrelated memory does not help: who_am_i is still refused. Every surface goes through egress.release (egress.py:500-504), so this hits Claude, GPT and the terminal alike.

scale.title: Read-only calls write the whole store and a snapshot, so the 20-snapshot safety net lasts about 19 tool calls
scale.repro: h/harness_b.py: with 10k facts, dispatch_tool('forget', {'contains': 'a'}) removes 9,991 facts. Then call dispatch_tool('priorities_for', ...) 19 times: no snapshot in conscience.history still holds the facts. h/harness_a.py shows every gated read does 1 full 6.33 MB write plus a snapshot copy.
scale.impact: An accidental or injected mass forget (by a confused engine or a scammer's prompt) can't be undone after a few minutes of ordinary use. For a dementia user, the family won't notice in time. Every question also rewrites the whole life twice: 12.7 MB per read at 10k facts and about 50 MB at 50k facts, which wears the drive and causes scale-24/25.
scale.fix: Stop calling _save() for access-log entries: keep that log in its own append-only JSONL (like egress), and do not log the ceiling check as a write. Keep snapshots on a time basis (for example hourly for 2 days, then daily for 60 days) instead of the last 20 writes. Require confirmation, or refuse, when forget/forget_life would remove more than a small number of entries.
scale.evidence: REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: f2_seed.py seeded 10,000 facts, then f2_run.py ran on the terminal surface (dispatch_tool). One priorities_for call: store rewritten=True, rev 1->3 (key provisioning plus the access-log entry), 3 snapshots. forget({'contains':'a'}) gave {'removed_facts': 10000}. Then repeated priorities_for: after 18 reads max_facts_in_any_snapshot=10000; after 19 reads max_facts_in_any_snapshot=0, with 20 snapshots holding no facts. Path: Gate.require -> check_access(log=True) -> _log -> c._save() (selfcloud.py:200-201, 207-212) -> _archive, which keeps the newest 20 (conscience.py:319-320). The code's own comment (conscience.py:35-36) says twenty snapshots 'buys back weeks of accidents'; in practice it buys back about 19 ordinary reads. ceiling() also logs and saves on every who_am_i/tell_story call (access.py:205).

scale.title: Whole-conscience payloads have no size cap: the system prompt, get_conscience, who_am_i and the local-engine history outgrow any context window
scale.repro: h/prompt_size.py: the system prompt is about 50 tokens per fact (106k tokens at 2,000 facts, 257k at 5,000, 508k at 10k). h/harness_b.py with a fake Ollama: one turn posts 2.29 MB, 2.29 MB, then 7.23 MB. h/harness_d_mcp.py: get_conscience 2.07 M chars, who_am_i 5.44 M chars. HTTP GET /life is 4.54 MB.
scale.impact: As the owner records his life, the terminal stops working with rented Claude at roughly 3,900 facts (an inference from the 200k window; the real API was not called). Hermes via Ollama is oversized even with an empty conscience (about 9.6k tokens), and the code sends no num_ctx. Claude and GPT get results far larger than one turn can hold. The owner's most-used product degrades exactly as it succeeds.
scale.fix: Put only top priorities, recent and relevant facts and counts in the system prompt, and fetch the rest by tool. Page get_conscience, who_am_i, tell_story and explain_basis (limit/offset, most relevant first). Enforce a per-tool byte budget in egress.release. For local engines, send options.num_ctx and trim old tool results from history.
scale.evidence: REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: f3_run.py with seeded stores. System prompt (jefferey_chat.py:1204-1214 dumps snapshot() with every fact, conscience.py:638-647): 0 facts = 14,354 chars plus 24,084 chars of tool JSON, so a 39,108-byte local POST (about 9.8k tokens at 4 chars/token). 2,000 facts = 368,797 chars (about 92k tokens). 5,000 facts = 902,900 chars (about 226k tokens), past a 200k window (inferred; no real API call). A fake Ollama turn calling who_am_i posted 1,012,655 bytes, then 1,948,039. The request carried only model/messages/tools, with no options or num_ctx (jefferey_chat.py:1351-1355), and history is never trimmed. At 5,000 facts and 500 memories: MCP get_conscience 888,652 chars, who_am_i 1,042,183, tell_story 153,579; HTTP /conscience 718,628 bytes, /life 827,123. egress.release (egress.py:482-508) has no size budget. The claim that Ollama truncates a ~10k-token prompt depends on its default context and could not be run here.

scale.title: A busy writer starves other surfaces: even read-only calls fail with ConscienceConflict, with no retry
scale.repro: h/harness_e2.py: the terminal runs review_statement(300 charges) on a 10k-fact store while the MCP process calls priorities_for every 0.5 s: 35 of 35 reads fail with UnexpectedToolError<-ConscienceConflict over 41.8 s. h/harness_e_two.py: MCP and terminal each write 60 facts at once, and MCP saves 0 of 60 while the terminal saves 60 of 60.
scale.impact: With two engines open, which the product promises, Claude Desktop returns generic 'Error executing tool' on every conscience question while the other engine is busy. Nothing is silently lost, but for a caregiver it looks broken.
scale.fix: Make reads not write (see the snapshot finding). Do mutations as reload-under-lock, apply, write, so a stale in-memory copy never conflicts, or retry on ConscienceConflict (refresh, re-apply, up to N tries) inside the surfaces' door wrappers.

scale.title: Write amplification: a statement review saves the whole store once per charge
scale.repro: h/harness_a.py: dispatch_tool('review_statement', 300 charges) on a 10k-fact store takes 38.7 s with 301 full-store writes and 1.92 GB written, plus as much in snapshot copies. h/harness_j.py: POST /charges/review with 1,000 charges takes 29.9 s even on a 1 MB store.
scale.impact: A caregiver reviewing a year of statements waits 40 s or more, writes gigabytes to the owner's SSD, wipes out the snapshot history in one call, and blocks every other engine for the whole time. GPT Actions are likely to time out on large statements.
scale.fix: In review_statement, call check_charge(record=False) per charge and append all the charges_seen entries with one _save(). Throttle _archive to at most one snapshot per minute. Longer term, keep append-heavy sections (charges_seen, actions, access log) in a journal or SQLite rather than one JSON blob.

scale.title: The egress log is not word for word once payloads pass 64 KB, but the report still says it is
scale.repro: After the large MCP run (h/harness_d_mcp.py), read d_large/egress.jsonl: 37.2 MB sent, 1.6 MB stored readable, 24 of 96 entries truncated. On a 1 MB store, 11 get_conscience sends are truncated. report() ends with 'Each one is in the log word for word.'
scale.impact: The privacy promise 'nothing leaves unlogged, read every send word for word' fails for the largest and most sensitive sends (whole life, whole conscience). The owner sees only a hash and a size for most of the bytes that left.
scale.fix: Cap payloads first (see the payload finding). Then store full bodies, compressed if needed, in a side file referenced by the sha256, or raise the cap. Have the report mark truncated entries and drop the 'word for word' claim for them.

scale.title: Photo resume and the watcher re-hash the entire library every time
scale.repro: h/harness_g_photos.py: a second cmd_build with nothing new reads and hashes all 3,000 files, and so does a cmd_watch --once pass. At 80k photos of about 3.5 MB each, that is about 280 GB per run, longer than the 300 s watch interval.
scale.impact: 'A second run on 80,000 photographs takes seconds' is wrong by orders of magnitude. The watcher keeps the drive and CPU busy indefinitely on a MacBook (battery, heat). The second go.py run also blocks the wall for hours while it finishes the library.
scale.fix: Before hashing, skip files whose (path, size, mtime) match a photos row, and hash only new or changed files. Open the wall first and index in the background, or keep applying --limit in increments.

scale.title: Album moments don't scale: home life merges into one multi-year 'moment', and each story stores every hash
scale.repro: h/harness_h_80k.py album on an 80k index: the top moment is 'Canada (Ottawa, Toronto) · Jan 2012–Dec 2025' with 48,251 photos. The prompt asks about all 48,251, and record() stores 3.28 MB of hashes in one memory, so conscience.json grows 3.67 MB.
scale.impact: The veteran is asked a meaningless first question instead of 'Afghanistan, October 2011'. Each story adds megabytes that are rewritten on every call and copied into 20 snapshots, which makes the write problems above worse.
scale.fix: Split clusters by a maximum span (for example 30 days) or by density, and treat the home country as a base, not a trip. Rank trips (places away from home) first. Pin a moment id and a sample of no more than about 50 ids, and resolve the full set from the index when needed.

scale.title: Recall resolves occasions, seasons and months without a year to the current year, even when that date is in the future
scale.repro: recall.parse('christmas at the kitchen table', known, date(2026,10,12)) gives a window of 2026-12-20..27, so recall.run returns 0 hits on an 80k index that covers 14 Christmases.
scale.impact: For most of the year, the family's most natural wall questions ('Christmas', 'summer', 'in June') return 'Nothing matched'.
scale.fix: When no year is given, use the most recent past occurrence, or match the month and day across all years.

scale.title: Unbounded growth: egress log, access log and snapshots, with reports loading everything into memory
scale.repro: h/harness_f_egress.py on 100k heavy entries (460 MB): peak RSS 1.23 GB, 'report --all --full' takes 13 s and outputs 438 MB. Access log: +163 bytes per gated call, never pruned. Snapshots: 128 MB at 10k facts, about 492 MB at 50k.
scale.impact: Gradual drive and memory pressure on the owner's Mac and the 512 GB product drive. The comment promising 'a few hundred kilobytes' for snapshots is misleading.
scale.fix: Rotate the egress log monthly and stream summaries instead of building a list. Move the access log out of the conscience and roll it up. Use time-based snapshot retention.

scale.title: triage_message money regex is quadratic on long digit/comma runs
scale.repro: Representative(c).triage_message('x','s','statement: ' + '1,'*8000) takes 3.96 s, and _MONEY.findall alone takes 4.13 s. Doubling the body quadruples the time.
scale.impact: A crafted or CSV-heavy email stalls triage for minutes and burns CPU. Other calls keep running, so there is no harm beyond the delay.
scale.fix: Use a bounded money pattern such as [$£€]\s?\d{1,3}(?:,\d{3})*(?:\.\d{2})? and scan only the first 20 KB of a body.

scale.title: A failed save leaves a partial .tmp and an in-memory store that differs from disk
scale.repro: h/harness_k.py full: with RLIMIT_FSIZE set to the store size + 2 KB, remember_fact raises EFBIG. The store is intact, but a 6.33 MB c.json.tmp remains, and memory holds the unsaved fact (10,001 vs 10,000 on disk).
scale.impact: On a nearly full drive, the leftover .tmp takes the remaining space. A fact the engine was told failed can quietly persist on the next successful save.
scale.fix: Unlink the .tmp file on any write error, and re-read from disk (or roll back the mutation) when _save raises.

seam.title: Owner controls (revocations, narrowed scopes, door-shut) live in whichever store home.py picked; when the drive is away they silently reset and private data leaves
seam.repro: h2_fallback.py: p1 (drive in) revoke gpt-raw, remove money.read, egress.shut(); move drive away; p2 new HTTP process: GET /conscience with the gpt-raw token -> 200 with 'Takes warfarin'; door shut? False.
seam.impact: A revoked engine reads health facts, and a shut door is open the next time the owner talks without the drive. Unplugging the drive, which the owner believes makes everything stop, triggers it.
seam.fix: Keep grants, revocations and the door switch in one owner-level place that does not depend on the drive (or refuse to start when the drive is expected but absent). Never auto-issue a preset key to a store that has a revocation history elsewhere. Default to refusing service when no drive is present once one has ever been provisioned.
seam.evidence: REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: Reproduced from scratch: hA.py (fresh HOME, home._mounts patched to a fake /Volumes so the drive is autodetected as on the Mac, HTTP TestClient). p0 with no drive: jefferey POST /facts 'Takes warfarin; INR checked monthly' went to home/.jefferey. p1 with the drive in: revoked gpt-raw, then GET /conscience -> 403 'key revoked'. Removed money.read from jefferey, then /charges/expected -> 403. egress.shut() -> is_shut True. p2 with the drive moved away and the server relaunched: root None; switch path home/.jefferey/door-shut, is_shut False. REVOKED gpt-raw GET /conscience -> 200 {facts:[{'fact':'Takes warfarin; INR checked monthly'}]}. jefferey /charges/expected -> 200. /selfcloud/grants shows money.read back on jefferey. Cause: home.py:65-87 and 106-110 fall back to ~/.jefferey; egress.py:312-317 checks only that store's switch; access.py:156-170 re-issues presets. This contradicts selfcloud.py:32-33 ('when the drive is off, none of this is reachable') and the drive's own rule at provision_drive.py:244. || IMPACT CONFIRMED: Reproduced (harness tmp.mgIIEWHrWK/h.py, home._mounts faked, HOME throwaway). p0 no drive: fact 'Takes warfarin' goes to home/.jefferey. p1 drive in: revoke gpt-raw, drop money.read, egress.shut(), giving gpt-raw /conscience 403 and money 403. p2 new process, drive away: gpt-raw 200 ['Takes warfarin...'], jefferey money 200, is_shut False. MCP with JEFFEREY_CLIENT=jefferey (the installer's Claude Desktop config, install.py:151-160, has no SELFCLOUD_ROOT): get_conscience returns warfarin with the door open. Causes: grants are stored in…

seam.title: Split-brain conscience and egress log: drive vs home folder, decided once per process, no merge, report incomplete
seam.repro: h3_late.py: start MCP before the drive exists, mount it, remember_fact -> stored in home/.jefferey. h2 p3: drive facts and home facts differ; the drive report omits 5 home-log sends.
seam.impact: Medical facts told while the drive was locked or away never reach the drive a caregiver or executor will read. 'What left the house' under-reports, including the revoked-key reads.
seam.fix: Re-resolve root() on each call, or refuse writes when no drive is present. Add a merge or import step on reconnect. Make report() read every known log location and flag the home-folder log.
seam.evidence: REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: hB.py [F1]: MCP started as jefferey with the fake /Volumes empty (root None). A marked Self-Cloud drive was then mounted and remember_fact('Allergic to penicillin') called. It was stored at $D/B1/home/.jefferey/conscience.json; the drive tree held only .selfcloud/selfcloud.json. describe() said 'on this machine (no Self-Cloud drive plugged in)' while the drive was mounted. hA.py p3, drive back: facts on drive ['Drive-era fact: new cardiologist Dr Patel']; facts at home ['Takes warfarin; INR checked monthly']. The drive egress log had 6 lines; the home log had 5 sends, including 2 gpt-raw get_conscience, one of them after the revoke. egress.entries()/report() read only log_path() (egress.py:376-377, 603-617, 657-664), so those sends never appear. A grep for merge/migrate/sync in connector/ and provision_drive.py finds nothing. home.py:66 says 'Decided once per process'. This breaks the drive's own rule 'no shadow copy elsewhere' (provision_drive.py:244).

seam.title: Drive identity is a marker file only: stranger drives adopted, clones indistinguishable, new ids unnoticed, node.json ignored
seam.repro: h4_marker.py with home._mounts patched: a stranger's marked drive alone -> conscience routed to it, and its facts served. A clone with the same id is adopted. Erase + re-provision -> new id, empty life, no warning. node.json-only drive -> not recognised.
seam.impact: The owner's life can be written onto someone else's drive, a stranger's life can be served to the owner's engine, and backup clones fork the conscience silently.
seam.fix: Record the drive id(s) the owner has accepted in an owner-side file and require confirmation for any new id. Add a role (primary/replica) to the marker and refuse writes to replicas. Settle selfcloud.json vs node.json by reading node.json's id when present.
seam.evidence: REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: hB.py, fresh HOME, fake /Volumes. [F2b] Only a stranger's marked drive (id ffff0000ffff0000) is mounted: root=USB-from-garage-sale. The owner's engine get_conscience returned "Mary's diagnosis: early Alzheimer's" plus a planted 'bank fraud line 1-800-555-0199' fact. The owner's remember_fact was written to the stranger's drive. [F2c] A clone with the same id, mounted alone, was adopted silently; the marker has no role field. [F2d] provision, then erase and re-provision: id ca4199b0... became 1c3e5a59..., get_conscience returned facts [] and no warning. A corrupt marker with force=True minted 03132988... ('kept? False'), despite the 'keeps the id' text at provision_drive.py:216. [F2e] A node.json-only drive gave root None and the home store. Cause: home.py:78-86 tests only that the marker file exists, and marker() is read only for the name (home.py:90-97, 141-147); no id is remembered anywhere. My rating is RISK, not FAIL: this matches the 'plug it in anywhere' design, but a planted drive becomes an injection path into the conscience for elderly users. || IMPACT CONFIRMED: Mechanics reproduced: with a stranger's marked drive as the only mount, root is that drive and the jefferey key is served ["Mary's diagnosis: early Alzheimer's"] (home.py:78-87 checks only that the marker exists). provision_drive on that second-hand drive prints 'already a Self-Cloud drive, Nothing changed' and leaves the stranger's conscience in place (provision_drive.py:208-217). With both drives plugged in, it uses neither and silently falls back to the home store. Much of the criti…

seam.title: Unplug does not stop a running process; refusals happen only as a side effect of the audit write
seam.repro: h1_unplug.py: shut the door, rename the drive dir away; ungated tools return results through an open door, logged to a ghost path. Gated reads fail with ConscienceConflict.
seam.impact: The stated security model ('unplug it') is not enforced. Moving the audit log out of the store, as the review recommends, would turn this into a full in-memory leak. Ghost directories may also disturb the remount.
seam.fix: Before every call, check the drive is still mounted (stat the marker) and fail closed with a clear 'drive unreachable' result. Never mkdir parents at the old mount path.
seam.evidence: REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: hB.py [F3], MCP as jefferey with a marked drive. remember_fact('Takes warfarin') ran, then egress.shut(); get_conscience was refused while shut. Renaming the drive dir away (the unplug) gave is_shut False. get_directives, selfcloud_status, selfcloud_grants, selfcloud_access_log and orb_state still returned results. get_conscience, remember_fact and what_left_the_house gave 'Error executing tool': ConscienceConflict from the audit _save (selfcloud.py:206-211 -> conscience.py:286-292); no check verifies the drive is present. m.conscience.data still held ['Takes warfarin']. A ghost tree appeared at the old mount: .selfcloud/jefferey/conscience.json.lock and egress.jsonl, with 5 sends logged there (egress.py:383-384, conscience.py:164,323). I rate it medium, not high: no private fact left in the repro, and what did leave was grants, the access log and the orb mood. Caveat: on a real Mac /Volumes is likely root-owned, so the ghost mkdir would probably fail and even ungated sends would error. I could not check that here.

seam.title: Guest keys can revoke or narrow other clients' keys, and the audit trail is ungated
seam.repro: h9_guest.py: claude-raw selfcloud_revoke('jefferey') -> revoked; the owner's Claude then gets AccessDenied. claude-raw reads selfcloud_access_log.
seam.impact: A prompt-injected guest can lock an elderly owner out of his caretaker until someone uses a terminal.
seam.fix: Allow a client to narrow only its own key, and require the owner console for anyone else's. Gate selfcloud_access_log, grants and status.

seam.title: Hard links in JEFFEREY's drive namespace redirect its writes (the §5.2 class)
seam.repro: h11_link.py: hard-link egress.jsonl to a file in the home folder; one tool call appends the egress log to that file.
seam.impact: Anything that can write to the mounted drive can steer JEFFEREY's logs into the owner's other files.
seam.fix: Before writing, check st_nlink==1 and the expected owner. Create files with O_EXCL plus O_NOFOLLOW and refuse pre-existing temp files.

seam.title: Two catalogs, two walkers, and the photo index stores absolute paths with no exclusions
seam.repro: Code reading only (that harness did not run): photo_index.py:272-290, 437-441, 612-636.
seam.impact: Re-hashes the whole library every pass, can index its own thumbnails or backups, loses photos after a remount, and declines stored in the index can be lost.
seam.fix: Finish B2/B3: read Self-Cloud's catalog by (node id, relative path, sha). Store drive-relative paths. Exclude .selfcloud and Backups.backupdb. Hash only on size/mtime change. Move moment decline status into the conscience.

seam.title: Seam decisions and safety asks unanswered; key work unowned
seam.repro: BUILD_JOURNAL.md has no laptop-agent entry after 2026-09-14. No backup verifier, no catalog door, no 6.1 sentence, no marker decision.
seam.impact: 80k photos with no verified second-copy gate. The erase runbook omits JEFFEREY's data. Encryption, backups and the kill switch belong to no running code.
seam.fix: Owner records B1/B6 and the marker decision in CANON. Assign the backup verifier. Add JEFFEREY's namespace to ENCRYPT §2c check 3.

seam.title: Second MCP servers bypass the egress door
seam.repro: Code and docs only: install.py:184-191 lists other servers by name; egress.py:5-6.
seam.impact: A filesystem or Self-Cloud door in Claude Desktop can read the conscience, voice and photos unlogged.
seam.fix: Have install.py inspect other servers' paths and refuse or warn loudly if they name the drive or home folder, and show this in 'What left the house'.
seam.evidence: REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: Executed tools/install.py wire_claude_desktop('jefferey') in a throwaway HOME. The existing claude_desktop_config.json had a 'filesystem' server with args [$HOME, '/Volumes/Self-Cloud']. Output: 'Left your other 1 connection(s) alone: filesystem', with no warning, and the args were kept unchanged (install.py:184-191; verify at 257-266 also checks only its own key). egress.py:13-17 covers only JEFFEREY's own registered tools. conscience.json and egress.jsonl, which holds the word-for-word sends, are plain JSON on the mounted drive or in ~/.jefferey, so any MCP server that names those paths reads them unlogged. START_HERE.md:103-108 warns about this in prose only. I could not see the owner's real filesystem folders or the Self-Cloud connector, so harm depends on his config. Rated medium because it is documented and conditional.

selling.title: authorize_action is ungated: any key, including revoked, unknown, family, executor and plain sessions, gets the caretaker's acting authority
selling.files: connector/jefferey_mcp.py:217-222; connector/jefferey_http.py:307-312; connector/access.py:59-101 (no TOOL_SCOPES entry); connector/conscience.py:478-531 (permissions are per category, not per client)
selling.repro: Owner console: Conscience(p).set_permission('selling','act',cap=500); SelfCloud(c).revoke('gpt-raw'). Then with JEFFEREY_HTTP_TOKENS='jefferey:tokA,gpt-raw:tokB,family:tokC,executor:tokD': TestClient(h.app).post('/actions/authorize', json={'category':'selling','description':'Accept $400','amount':400}, headers={'Authorization':'Bearer tokB'}) returns 200 {allowed:true}. The same holds for tokC and tokD, and on MCP for JEFFEREY_CLIENT=claude-raw, executor and some-random-agent.
selling.impact: authorize_action is the only code-level control behind 'never sends or signs without authorize_action'. A revoked Custom GPT, an executor key meant only for legacy, or a plain Claude session gets the same 'allowed' as the caretaker, then acts through Gmail, R-evolv or a browser. Revocation does not revoke acting authority.
selling.fix: Gate authorize_action with a dedicated scope (e.g. 'act.request') held only by 'jefferey', and deny revoked or unknown keys. Key permissions by (client, category). Return a single-use authorization id bound to client, category, amount, description and expiry, and log it.
selling.evidence: REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: Fresh dir $D/s1. Owner setup: set_permission('selling','act',cap=500); SelfCloud grant presets; revoke('gpt-raw'). HTTP (TestClient, tokens jefferey:tokA,gpt-raw:tokB,family:tokC,executor:tokD) POST /actions/authorize {selling,'Accept $400',400}: tokA, tokB (REVOKED), tokC, tokD all returned 200 {allowed:true,'within granted authority'}. Control: POST /actions (log_action, @gate facts.write) with tokB gave 403 "key revoked". MCP with JEFFEREY_CLIENT=claude-raw, executor, some-random-agent, gpt-raw: authorize_action -> allowed:true for every one, while log_action -> refused for every one. Code: jefferey_mcp.py:217-222 and jefferey_http.py:307-312 have no @gate; access.py TOOL_SCOPES has no authorize_action entry; conscience.py:478-531 holds permissions per category, not per client. So revoking a key does not take away its acting authority. A hostile engine could skip the check anyway, but a cooperative revoked or arm's-length engine is told it may act.

selling.title: In the owner's terminal the model can raise its own authority: OWNER_CONSOLE is set for the whole process and set_permission is a model tool
selling.repro: h1b_local.py: a fake OpenAI server on 127.0.0.1:0 returns tool_call set_permission {category:selling, level:act}, then authorize_action {selling, $50 for the Civic}. jc.run_turn_local(history) leaves conscience.permission_for('selling') == 'act' and authorize returns allowed:true. No human confirmation at any step.
selling.impact: 'Jefferey never widens Jefferey' is enforced only by prompt on the surface the owner trusts most, the owned local model, and small local models are the easiest to inject. A buyer email pasted in for advice can turn on selling with no cap. Anyone at the unlocked Mac counts as the owner.
selling.fix: Remove set_permission, selfcloud_grant and selfcloud_add_scope from the model's tool list in jefferey_chat. Make widening a typed slash-command (e.g. '/allow selling act 500') handled outside the model loop, or have dispatch_tool block on input('Raise selling to act, no cap? type YES') for OWNER_ONLY_TOOLS. Optionally add a local passcode.
selling.evidence: REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: $D/s2 chat_local.py, with JEFFEREY_OWNER_CONSOLE unset in the env. Output: 'env OWNER_CONSOLE before import: None' / 'after import: 1 client: jefferey' (jefferey_chat.py:64 setdefault). A fake OpenAI server on 127.0.0.1:0 scripted set_permission{selling,act} and then authorize_action{selling,'Accept $50 for the Civic'}. After jc.run_turn_local, the user turn was an injected buyer email. Results: TOOL set_permission -> {level:act,cap:null}; authorize_action -> allowed:true; permission_for('selling') went from 'recommend' to {'level':'act','cap':None}. dispatch_tool (jefferey_chat.py:892-893) only checks the env var, so there is no human confirmation. The only sign is a dim trace line, '· authority: selling → act'. set_permission is in the model's TOOLS (line 199). So 'Jefferey never widens Jefferey' rests on the prompt alone on this surface.

selling.title: The spending cap is bypassed by leaving out the amount, sending a negative amount, or sending NaN
selling.files: connector/conscience.py:515; connector/jefferey_http.py:301-304 (ActionAskIn.amount float); connector/jefferey_chat.py:1381 (json.loads accepts NaN)
selling.repro: c.set_permission('selling','act',cap=500); c.authorize_action('selling','Sell the 2015 Civic for $8,000') -> allowed. Same with amount=-8000 or amount=float('nan'). Over HTTP, body '{..."amount":NaN}' -> 200 allowed.
selling.impact: The one numeric safeguard is defeated by leaving out a field. The same code guards 'purchases', so this is money-adjacent beyond selling.
selling.fix: If a cap exists, require amount. Reject amounts that are not finite (math.isfinite) or are negative. Use Field(ge=0, allow_inf_nan=False) in the HTTP and MCP schemas, and refuse NaN from local-model JSON (json.loads parse_constant raising).
selling.evidence: REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: $D/s3 core.py with set_permission('selling','act',cap=500). authorize_action('selling','Sell the 2015 Civic for $8,000') with no amount -> True; with -8000 -> True; with nan -> True; with 8000 -> False (control); inf -> False. A string amount raises TypeError. HTTP with tokA, raw bodies: no amount, amount -8000 and amount NaN each gave 200 allowed:true; amount 8000 gave allowed:false. MCP (claude-raw) with float('nan') and -8000 -> allowed:true. Cause: conscience.py:515 only compares when amount is not None, and NaN > cap is False. Because the amount is self-reported, a lying engine could also just state a low figure. The real harm is an honest or sloppy engine (small local models often drop optional fields) slipping past the cap.

selling.title: No sale-shaped controls: the cap is a ceiling with no floor, the category is chosen by the model, items have no state, and there is no second approver
selling.repro: set_permission('selling','act',500); authorize_action('selling','Sell the ring (appraised $4,200) for $20',20) three times -> all allowed. set_permission('correspondence','act'); authorize_action('correspondence','Accept $200 for the Civic',200) -> allowed. Two processes each log 'Oak table sold' to different buyers -> both stored.
selling.impact: For elderly and dementia users this is the financial-abuse path: a scammer or a confused moment sells a valuable for almost nothing, the same item gets sold twice, or a sale is approved under an unrelated permission. Nothing notices.
selling.fix: Add a sale act type: item id, an owner-set floor price, and a state machine (listed, pending, sold) that refuses a second sale. Map categories to allowed verbs so correspondence cannot accept a sale. Add an optional co-approver (a named caregiver) and a cooling-off period above a value threshold.
selling.evidence: REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: $D/s3 core.py with selling act cap=500. 'Sell the ring (appraised $4,200) for $20',20 was allowed three times in a row. 'Sell the ring for $600' was DENIED, so for a sale the cap blocks the better price and lets the lowball through. With correspondence at act, authorize_action('correspondence','Accept $200 for the Civic',200) -> True, because the category is a free string the caller picks (conscience.py:501-519). An unknown category is denied by default (correct). Two processes log_action 'Oak table sold to Alice' and '...to Bob': both stored, since there is no item state. The cap inversion and the free-text category are real design risks for elderly users. Both need the owner to grant act first. 'No item state' and 'no co-approver' are missing features rather than defects (marketplace tools carry their own sold state), so I rate this medium, not high.

selling.title: Audit trail gaps: approvals are not logged, log_action takes unverified claims, and a shut door still lets writes happen while telling the model 'refused'
selling.repro: 3 allowed authorize_action calls add 0 action-log entries. log_action('estate_sale','Sold Dad\'s medals... $9,000','completed') is accepted while estate_sale is 'recommend'. egress.shut(); dispatch_tool('log_action',...) returns refused, but the entry is stored.
selling.impact: The owner cannot tell from his own log what was approved, or whether a recorded sale was ever authorized. A model told 'refused' may retry and write duplicates.
selling.fix: Log allowed verdicts with an authorization id. Have log_action require that id, or record outcome 'UNAUTHORIZED' visibly. Check is_shut() before running a tool, or report the write truthfully.

selling.title: Scam triage misses most seller-side scams
selling.repro: rep.triage_message('b','Guitar','Can I pay with Apple gift cards?') -> routine 0.0. Also routine: courier/oil-rig pickup, the 6-digit verification-code request, fake Purchase Protection link, French overpayment cheque, request for a licence photo, 'home alone' question, zero-width or obfuscated text.
selling.impact: This is the only protective tool in the selling flow, and it tells the model 'Handle quietly. Do not interrupt the user' on the scams that hit Marketplace sellers: phone and account takeover by verification code, overpayment, fake payment, identity theft, and casing a senior's home.
selling.fix: Add a seller-scam signal set: overpayment and refund-the-difference, courier or shipping-agent pickup, verify-you're-real codes, claim-funds links, business-account upgrades, ID-document requests, porch or mailbox payment, schedule or home-alone questions, and instruction-like text aimed at the assistant. Use inflection-tolerant regexes (gift cards?). NFKC-normalise and strip zero-width characters and de-obfuscate before matching. Add French patterns. Add a selling context mode.
selling.evidence: REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: $D/s4 triage.py, rep.triage_message(...). 'Can I pay with Apple gift cards?' -> routine 0.0 ('Handle quietly. Do not interrupt the user'), while singular 'a gift card' -> suspicious 0.35. The plural fails because of the trailing \b in representative.py:72. Also routine 0.0: oil-rig courier pickup with refund of the courier fee; 'text me back the 6-digit code to prove you're real'; fake FB Purchase Protection claim link; French overpayment cheque; request for a driver's licence photo; 'will you be home alone'; zero-width obfuscated 'g​ift c​ard ... ur​gent'. The English overpayment cheque came back needs_decision with scam_score 0.0. Control: the classic 'URGENT account suspended verify identity click here' -> likely_scam 0.55. The signal list (representative.py:67-92) has no seller-side patterns, and an explicit 'do not interrupt' verdict can suppress the model's own warning.

selling.title: A secret-shaped string in a buyer message switches off triage entirely, and scammers can trigger it on purpose
selling.repro: dispatch_tool('triage_message', {'body': '<PayPal-agent scam text> PayPal ref 4111 1111 1111 1111'}) -> refused at the door, no verdict. 'the password is couch' does the same.
selling.impact: Any scammer can disable the scam screen by adding a fake card number or 'password: x'. Honest e-transfer messages that include the security answer cannot be triaged either. The model is told to say the door kept it and stop.
selling.fix: triage_message stores nothing, so mask matched spans and continue instead of refusing at admit. Treat a secret-shaped string or code in an inbound message as a scam signal in its own right.
selling.evidence: REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: $D/s5 f6_chat.py, jc.dispatch_tool('triage_message', ...). The PayPal-agent/Western Union scam text plus ' PayPal ref 4111 1111 1111 1111' -> REFUSED 'contains what looks like a card number', with tell_the_user 'Say plainly that the egress door kept this in the house, and stop.' The same text without the ref -> suspicious. 'Sent the e-transfer for the couch, the password is couch' -> REFUSED (password); 'the answer is couch' -> suspicious. MCP (JEFFEREY_CLIENT=jefferey, $D/s6) gives the same refused:true. Cause: egress.admit (egress.py:457-479, called at line 576 and at jefferey_chat.py:896) scans tool inputs even though triage stores nothing and the engine already holds the text. A scammer can kill the scam verdict with a Luhn-valid number. Rated medium, not high: the model is not told the message is 'routine', and it still has the text to judge itself.

selling.title: Triage flags honest e-transfer buyers and never looks at the sender
selling.repro: Same Interac notice from someone@example.invalid and from someone@example.invalid: identical result (suspicious 0.3). 'I can send an Interac e-Transfer for $400 tonight' -> suspicious.
selling.impact: It steers sellers away from the safest way to get paid and cannot tell the real Interac sender from a lookalike. That trains users to ignore warnings.
selling.fix: Score direction ('send me / you must pay' versus 'I will send you'). Score sender domains: allow-list real Interac and bank domains, flag lookalikes.

selling.title: Identity-theft-grade identifiers are accepted, stored, released to arm's-length keys and auto-filled into any form
selling.files: connector/representative.py:57-63 (SENSITIVE_PATTERNS lacks licence/license, passport, maiden name, health card), 125-140; connector/egress.py:216-244
selling.repro: rep.set_profile_field("Driver's licence number",'C6101-40706-60905') -> stored. With JEFFEREY_CLIENT=claude-raw, MCP get_profile returns it. fill_form for a fake escrow form fills date of birth, address, phone, email and mother's maiden name.
selling.impact: Contradicts 'sensitive identifiers are never stored or auto-filled'. These are exactly the fields scam 'seller verification' and escrow forms ask for. A plain Claude or GPT session can read them.
selling.fix: Add licence/license, passport, health card, maiden name, place of birth and security question to SENSITIVE_PATTERNS so they go vault-only. Add egress shapes for provincial licence formats. Warn whenever date of birth plus address go to a form that is not government.
selling.evidence: REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: $D/s7 f89_setup.py: set_profile_field stored "Driver's licence number"='C6101-40706-60905' and 'Passport number'='AB123456' (stored:True). MCP JEFFEREY_CLIENT=claude-raw get_profile returned both values. Partly refuted: 'Health card number' was REFUSED (it contains 'card number'), so health cards are already covered. fill_form did NOT auto-fill the licence (it went to needs_you). 'Mother's maiden name' is not leaked as a maiden name: it maps to full_name (see #9), so the field gets the owner's name, or the maiden name only after it has overwritten full_name. DOB, address, phone and email filling is by design. What stands: licence and passport numbers go into the profile and out to plain Claude/GPT sessions through facts.read (SENSITIVE_PATTERNS, representative.py:57-63). Medium, not high.

selling.title: Field matching maps any label containing 'name', 'address' or 'phone' to the owner's own fields
selling.repro: fill_form(['Buyer name','Buyer address','Buyer phone','Lienholder name']) -> all filled with the owner's details. set_profile_field('Buyer name','Mike Ross') -> stored as full_name, and draft_guidance then gives write_as 'Mike Ross'.
selling.impact: A car bill of sale lists the seller as the buyer, which can leave him liable for the vehicle. Storing a buyer's or a pet's name silently renames the owner, and every later draft is signed with someone else's name.
selling.fix: Drop loose containment for generic aliases (name, address, phone, first, last). Never map labels with a party or qualifier (buyer, purchaser, lienholder, company, pet, mother's, user) to owner fields. For set_profile_field, require an exact alias match or refuse.
selling.evidence: REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: $D/s7 f89_setup.py. fill_form(['Buyer name','Buyer address','Buyer phone','Lienholder name']) -> all filled with the owner's full_name, address_line1 and phone (the loose containment pass at representative.py:436-439). set_profile_field('Buyer name','Mike Ross') -> {'stored':True,'field':'full_name'}, which silently overwrote the owner's name. draft_guidance(...)['write_as'] -> 'Mike Ross'. Worse, set_profile_field("Mother's maiden name",'Kovacs') also overwrote full_name, so every later form ('Seller full name': 'Kovacs') and claude-raw get_profile showed the wrong name. The result is silent corruption of the owner's identity and drafts signed under another person's name. A bill of sale can list the seller as the buyer.

selling.title: From Claude Desktop the owner cannot narrow a permission ('stop selling'), and the reason is lost
selling.files: connector/access.py:23-26, 105, 274-288; connector/jefferey_mcp.py:62-76 (only EgressRefused becomes a result)
selling.repro: MCP set_permission {'category':'selling','level':'observe'} without the console -> 'Error executing tool set_permission'.
selling.impact: In the middle of a scam, the owner or a caregiver cannot shut off selling from the app he actually uses. The model cannot explain why.
selling.fix: Allow set_permission when the new level is lower or the cap smaller. Convert OwnerOnly and AccessDenied into result dicts in the MCP door, as already done for egress refusals.

selling.title: Any key, including revoked and family keys, can flood the owner's action log and push every recovery snapshot out
selling.repro: 30 HTTP authorize_action calls with the family token: action_log top 20 all noise, 0 of 13 earlier snapshots survive. 22 denied explain_basis calls from a revoked gpt-raw: 0 of 13 survive.
selling.impact: Real sale records are buried in the owner's view, and the 20-write rollback window can be used up in seconds by a client that has no rights. A bad write (e.g. selling-83) then cannot be rolled back.
selling.fix: Keep access-check and denial logs in a separate append-only file outside the snapshot cadence, aggregate repeated denials, and rate-limit denied clients. Keep snapshots by time (daily for 30 days) rather than by count.

selling.title: The owner's selling priorities and item facts are not found for natural requests
selling.repro: set_priority('selling',...) and remember_fact('The Civic has 142,000 km...'); draft_guidance('sell my 2015 Honda Civic on Marketplace') returns 0 priorities and 0 facts.
selling.impact: Listings and replies are drafted without the owner's values (e.g. safe pickup over highest price), and the model honestly answers 'I don't know your values'.
selling.fix: Match on tokens and stems (sell, selling, sale; civic) or on category tags. Have draft_guidance also return the disclosure and representation rules for the recipient audience.

selling.title: The egress scanner blocks harmless tracking numbers but lets one-time codes through
selling.repro: log_action(description='... tracking 7023210039414605') -> refused as a card number. looks_secret('Your Marketplace login code is 482913') -> None.
selling.impact: Shipping records are lost about 10% of the time. The verification-code scam's payload, the code itself, is not treated as a secret.
selling.fix: Require card context (keywords or BIN ranges) and exempt digit runs labelled tracking/order/ref. Add OTP patterns ('code (is|:) \d{4,8}', 'verification/confirmation/login code') to looks_secret in both directions.

selling.title: No incoming-money side: payment arrival cannot be confirmed, deposits look like unexpected charges, and there is no seller chargeback pack
selling.repro: review_statement([{'merchant':'INTERAC E-TRANSFER FROM M ROSS','amount':-400},{'merchant':'E-TRANSFER DEPOSIT M ROSS','amount':400}]) -> both 'unexpected_merchant', '$0.00 at stake'. dispute_pack('Mike Ross (buyer)') -> empty, with merchant-refund advice.
selling.impact: The most common seller loss, handing over the item on a fake payment confirmation, has no defence. After-sale chargebacks have no support.
selling.fix: Add expected_payment(item, buyer, amount, method), marked received only when the owner confirms in his bank app (never from an email or screenshot), plus the rule 'do not release the item until it shows in your bank'. Add a seller-side dispute pack: messages, pickup receipt, photos.

selling.title: R-evolv (the marketplace connector in the same Claude account) sits entirely outside JEFFEREY's doors and keeps personal data in its own cloud 'Self Cloud'
selling.files: No R-evolv code in connector/ or tools/ (grep). R-evolv server instructions loaded in this session. directives.md:33-38, 196-202
selling.repro: Not executed (forbidden to call). With both connectors in Claude Desktop, create_listing, send_message, mark_sold and create_checkout run without authorize_action, egress logging or the shut switch. Its instructions tell the model to save 'their town, budgets, what they own' to 'SupplAi's Self Cloud' at r-evolv.com, to treat a card-button click as consent to message or check out, and to send email and phone alerts in the background.
selling.impact: 'Nothing leaves unlogged', 'never sends without authorize_action' and 'the drive is the product' do not hold for the very connector that sells. A list of valuables plus a town in a third-party cloud is a burglary map. Users, especially elderly ones, will think 'Self Cloud' means their own drive.
selling.fix: Rename R-evolv's memory so it cannot be mistaken for Self-Cloud. Route marketplace acts through a JEFFEREY proxy tool that calls authorize_action and egress, or do not install R-evolv in the same profile. Add a directive that third-party connectors do not hold the owner's memory. Make R-evolv honour the shut switch.
selling.evidence: REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: Did not call R-evolv. Traced the code and ran what I could. (1) grep -rniE 'revolv|supplai' over both repos finds no code. Revolv shows up only in docs, as a future import source (FOUNDER_DIRECTIONS.md:108,118). (2) R-evolv's server instructions are loaded in this session, which runs on the same claude.ai account. They say: 'MEMORY LIVES IN REVOLV — SupplAi's Self Cloud is the memory bank for... their town, budgets, what they own'. They say 'Do not keep Revolv preferences only in your own platform's memory'. They treat the card button as 'the person choosing — take them straight to the deal (send_message... or create_checkout)'. They promise 'email and phone alert' from the cloud. (3) I ran it: jefferey_mcp's m.mcp.instructions prints None. JEFFEREY's directives reach the model only if it calls get_directives (jefferey_mcp.py:96-101), while R-evolv's instructions load every time. (4) egress.py:4-9 and 33-36 limit the door and the shut switch to what JEFFEREY itself hands out ('JEFFEREY's own switch'). The egress log I produced records only engine 'Anthropic (Claude)'. If the model passes a released fact on to R-evolv, nothing on the drive records that second hop. (5) directives.md says nothing about other connectors. Caveat: R-evolv looks like the owner's own product ('REVOLV Self Cloud spec', DIGITAL_CONSCIENCE_ARCHITECTURE.md:51), and I could not see what create_checkout really does.

selling.title: Buyer-facing drafts are never checked against disclosure rules; physical-safety facts are readable and pickup safety is absent
selling.files: connector/representative.py:364-389; connector/rules.py:133-171 (works only when the model calls it); connector/selfcloud.py:62-66 (claude-raw facts.read)
selling.repro: remember_fact('Lives alone since 2024; home most weekdays'); claude-raw get_conscience returns it. draft_guidance(...) has no disclosure field. check_disclosure('buyer','lives alone') -> false, but only if the model asks.
selling.impact: An elderly seller living alone can end up telling a stranger when he is home alone, and the scam screen does not flag strangers who ask (selling-20).
selling.fix: Add check_draft(text, audience) that scans a draft against deny rules and tagged sensitive facts before it is shown. Put disclosure verdicts in draft_guidance. Ship safety defaults for pickup: public exchange zone, never share schedule or who lives there, a record of who is coming.
selling.evidence: REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: Fresh HOME and temp dir. Owner terminal (jc.dispatch_tool) stored remember_fact('Lives alone since 2024; home most weekdays'). It then set a disclosure rule: tags 'lives alone, schedule, home', audience anyone, allow False. MCP as JEFFEREY_CLIENT=claude-raw gave: get_conscience still has fact: True (the egress log shows it went to Claude). draft_guidance('reply to a buyer about pickup at my home','buyer') returns keys [purpose, recipient, rules, their_facts_here, their_priorities_here, voice, write_as]: no disclosure verdict, and the deny rule never appears (representative.py:364-389 never looks at rules). check_disclosure('buyer','lives alone') returns allowed False, but only when the model chooses to call it. triage_message('What's your address and when are you usually home alone?') returns routine 0.0, 'Handle quietly. Do not interrupt the user for this.' 'come when it's just you. Send me the address.' gets the same result. Of 64 MCP tools, none checks a draft or covers pickup safety. Lowering factors: claude-raw facts.read is intended (selfcloud.py:62-66), and JEFFEREY does not send by itself. The chain runs on what the model and the owner do, but the scam screen tells the engine to keep a home-casing message away from the owner.

selling.title: Most of the selling pipeline does not exist: listing, pricing, SMS, shipping and records
selling.files: connector/jefferey_chat.py TOOLS (62 tools, none for selling)
selling.repro: [t['name'] for t in jc.TOOLS] has no listing, offer, payment, SMS or shipping tool.
selling.impact: Today JEFFEREY can only triage, draft guidance and gate. Every real selling step happens in other connectors, outside the doors (see the R-evolv finding).
selling.fix: Decide deliberately: either build listing, offer, sale and payment tools inside the doors, or make JEFFEREY the gate and log for an external marketplace through a proxy. Add sale records with cost basis for tax.

selling.title: No decommission path when the owner sells the Mac or the drive
selling.repro: No wipe or decommission command in connector/ or tools/.
selling.impact: The conscience, 20 history snapshots, the egress log (buyer messages word for word) and MCP config tokens go to the next owner unless he knows to erase by hand.
selling.fix: Add 'Prepare this Mac/drive for sale': revoke all keys, delete store, history, egress log and the MCP config entry, clear vault entries, and confirm FileVault/APFS erase.

selling.title: Listing photos can carry the home's GPS location
selling.repro: Not executed: there is no listing upload path in JEFFEREY. photo_index reads GPS and nothing strips it.
selling.impact: Item photos taken at home reveal the home's location once uploaded through any marketplace connector.
selling.fix: Strip EXIF and GPS from any photo handed out for a listing, and say so.

selling.title: No awareness of regulated items (firearms, military kit)
selling.repro: No rule or check exists.
selling.impact: A veteran owner could be helped toward an unlawful transfer.
selling.fix: Add a regulated-items list that refuses to draft or authorize and points to the lawful process.

selling.title: Replies are signed as the owner with no AI disclosure
selling.repro: draft_guidance -> write_as 'Laszlo Czako'.
selling.impact: Buyers may object, and marketplace terms may restrict automated messaging.
selling.fix: Add an owner-chosen disclosure setting (e.g. 'sent with help from my assistant').

texting.title: Scam triage misses about 70% of realistic Canadian scam texts and tells the engine they are real
texting.files: connector/representative.py:67-92 (signal regexes), :108 (money regex), :324-342 (verdict ladder and advice)
texting.repro: $D/run.sh g1 h1_triage.py. Result: false negatives 25/37 in the corpus; adding the h2/h7/h8 extras gives 31 of 44 scam texts not flagged. Examples: tri('please buy gift cards for me') -> routine (vs 'a gift card' -> suspicious); "don't tell your mother" -> routine; 'we suspended your account' -> routine 0.2; '407ETR unpaid toll $14.86 pay by Oct 14' -> needs_decision with advice 'Real and actionable'.
texting.impact: This is the core protective promise for elderly and dementia users, and it fails on the commonest Canadian frauds: grandchild 'new number', gift cards (plural), Canada Post/407/Hydro fees, any French text, Apple/Microsoft, SIN suspended, 'read me the code' takeovers. 10 scams come back as needs_decision ('Real and actionable. Recommend') and 15 as routine ('Handle quietly. Do not interrupt the user'). So the tool actively lends the scam credibility and suppresses the warning. That matters most with a small local model, which leans on tool output. Root causes: (a) word-boundary bugs: 'gift card\b' misses 'cards', and only 'do not tell' is matched, not "don't tell"; (b) English only, and money in '1 250,00 $' format is not recognised; (c) single signals weighted 0.10-0.20, under the 0.25 threshold; (d) the ladder ranks 'money mentioned' above present scam flags; (e) no URL or lookalike-domain check, no sender or contact awareness, no normalisation of leetspeak or homoglyphs; (f) no signals for code requests, wrong-number openers, 'new number', remote access ('connect to your PC'), crypto slang (BTC, USDT, 'guaranteed returns').
texting.fix: (1) Fix the regexes now: 'gift ?cards?', 'google play cards?', "(?:do not|don't|dont) tell", "you(?:'ve| have)? won|u won", 'lott(?:ery|o)', 'btc|usdt|crypto', '(?:account|card|sin).{0,20}(?:suspended|locked|disabled)'. (2) Normalise first: NFKC, map Cyrillic and Greek confusables, de-leet 0->o, 3->e. (3) Add French signal and money patterns (urgent, immédiatement, mandat d'arrêt, suspendu, vérifier votre identité, frais, '\d[\d  ]*,\d{2} ?\$'). (4) Add URL signals: any link in an unsolicited text, non-.ca/.gc.ca domains naming CRA/Canada Post/banks, digit-for-letter brand spellings, shorteners (bit.ly, t.me). (5) Add signals for 'reply with the code', 'new number', wrong-number openers, 'connect to your computer', bail/hospital plus money, government benefit plus banking details. (6) Change the ladder: any scam flag plus money or a link is at least suspicious; never print 'Real and actionable' when scam_flags is non-empty. (7) Use the sender: unknown number plus a claimed relationship is a flag. (8) Keep corpus.py (52 texts) as a regression test with false-negative and false-positive thresholds.
texting.evidence: REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: Reproduced from scratch with my own 16-text corpus of Canadian scams, written separately from the tester's. Run through the terminal surface: fresh HOME, jc.dispatch_tool('triage_message',...), harness $D/g1_triage.py with D=scratchpad/tmp.D2vdQiYsQM. Result: 14 of 16 scams were not flagged. 'new number' Mom text, grandchild bail with "don't tell Mom" + Google Play cards, RBC 'account has been locked', SIN suspended, wrong-number opener, Apple, 'send me the code back', French Postes Canada, 'buy gift cards', and the Microsoft 'connect to your PC' text all came back routine ('Handle quietly. Do not interrupt the user'). Canada Post $3.99, 407ETR $14.86, CRA refund and Hydro One disconnect came back needs_decision ('Real and actionable. Recommend'). Only the Amazon text (0.45) and the USDT text (0.3) were flagged suspicious. The tester's examples hold exactly: 'gift cards' gives routine but 'a gift card' gives suspicious 0.35; "don't tell" gives routine but 'do not tell' gives suspicious; 'we suspended your account' gives routine 0.2. 'URGENT: pay the $14.86 toll now' gives needs_decision with a scam flag present and the advice 'Real and actionable'. Causes are at representative.py:67-92 (narrow English-only regexes, gift card\b), the single weights under 0.25 at :329, and the ladder at :337, where money or a deadline beats scam flags.

texting.title: The egress door blocks triage of the most dangerous texts and tells the model to stop instead of warning
texting.files: connector/egress.py:216-244 (looks_secret), :457-479 (admit), :556-563 (refusal_result tell_the_user); connector/jefferey_chat.py:897, :1463-1469; jefferey_mcp.py/jefferey_http.py door wrappers
texting.repro: $D/run.sh g2 h2_door.py. Section B: triage of 'Interac: your security code is 551203. If you did not request it, call 1-833-...' -> refused, tell_the_user='Say plainly that the egress door kept this in the house, and stop.' Section C: the owner pasting the same text in the terminal gets the whole turn dropped. Section D: 11.2% of random 16-digit tracking numbers and 10.3% of 9-digit order numbers refused as card/SIN.
texting.impact: Texts that carry a secret-shaped string are exactly the account-takeover and credential-harvest attacks: a real bank code plus a caller asking for it, a fake card receipt, a 'confirm your SIN' text. For these the protective tool never runs, and the engine is told to stop, with a false reason ('does not take secrets into the conscience... nothing was stored', though triage stores nothing). An elderly owner pasting a text mid-scam gets a technical line about 'the egress door' and no warning. About 1 in 10 ordinary delivery texts are also un-triageable. The door protects nothing here: on MCP and GPT the host already holds the text, and triage_message returns no body.
texting.fix: Give triage_message a door exception that runs locally on the full text, then releases only the verdict fields, which already contain no body. Mask secret-shaped spans in the logged 'asked' instead of refusing. When a scan does hit, return a protective result rather than 'stop', e.g. {verdict:'likely_scam', advice:'This message contains a code/card/SIN. Never read it to anyone who calls or texts; hang up and call the number on your card.'}. On the terminal, when release_text refuses a paste, run triage locally and print the warning to the owner instead of only '(kept in the house)'. Make the SIN/card scans context-aware (require 'SIN'/'card' nearby, skip 'tracking/order/ref/#') to cut the ~10% Luhn false positives.
texting.evidence: REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: Harness $D/g2_door.py, a fresh process per surface. Terminal dispatch_tool('triage_message') on 'Interac: your security code is 551203. If you did not request it, call 1-833...' was refused: 'body ... looks like a password or PIN. JEFFEREY does not take secrets into the conscience... nothing was stored', with tell_the_user 'Say plainly that the egress door kept this in the house, and stop' (egress.py:556-563). A 'confirm your SIN 046 454 286' text and a 'parcel 4532015112830366' text were refused the same way. MCP (jefferey key) gave the same refusal result. HTTP /triage returned 403. The owner pasting the text at the terminal got release_text refused, so the owner sees only '(kept in the house ...)' and no warning (jefferey_chat.py:1463-1468). Triage stores nothing (facts after = 0), so the 'nothing was stored' reason is beside the point. On MCP and GPT the host engine already holds the text, so the refusal protects nothing. Ordinary numbers are refused too: 8.8% of random 16-digit tracking numbers and 10.2% of random 9-digit order numbers (n=2000 each) trip the Luhn card/SIN scans (egress.py:216-244). I rate this medium, not high: on MCP and GPT the engine can still warn on its own, and keeping an OTP out of a rented engine on the terminal follows the stated principle. What is missing is a local warning.

texting.title: Any engine on the owner's terminal can widen its own authority, and the widening persists to every surface
texting.files: connector/jefferey_chat.py:63-64 (setdefault JEFFEREY_OWNER_CONSOLE=1), :199-215 (set_permission exposed to the engine), :892-893; connector/access.py:274-288 (owner_only is an env check); connector/conscience.py:478-493
texting.repro: $D/run.sh g3 h3_send.py: jc.dispatch_tool('set_permission', {'category':'correspondence','level':'act'}) -> succeeds; authorize_action -> allowed True. A separate MCP process (claude-raw, no owner console) on the same conscience then gets authorize_action('correspondence') -> allowed true. $D/run.sh g6 h6_local.py: a scam SMS with an injected instruction, followed by a (simulated) obedient local model, gives payments=act with no cap, persisted.
texting.impact: 'JEFFEREY never moves money and never sends or signs without authorize_action' rests on authorize_action, and the engine can flip it. 'Owner console' is a property of the process, not a human decision. Every tool call from Claude or a small local Hermes in that terminal counts as 'the owner's own hands'. A pasted scam text carrying an injection is a realistic trigger. The raised level is stored in the shared conscience, so Claude Desktop, which may hold other connectors that can send mail or messages, then sees allowed:true.
texting.fix: Remove set_permission, selfcloud_grant and selfcloud_add_scope from the engine-facing TOOLS on every surface. Make widening a human-only slash command (/permit correspondence act) or a y/N prompt typed at the keyboard, outside the model loop (input() in chat(), never from dispatch_tool). Record who widened and from which surface. Also expire 'act' grants (e.g. 24 h) and require a per-act confirmation for correspondence and payments.
texting.evidence: REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: Harness $D/g3_widen.py, run with JEFFEREY_OWNER_CONSOLE unset. Importing jefferey_chat sets it to 1 (jefferey_chat.py:64 setdefault). Terminal: authorize_action('correspondence') gave False before; then dispatch_tool('set_permission',{'category':'correspondence','level':'act'}) was accepted with no human confirmation, and authorize_action gave True. A simulated obedient local model (fake OpenAI server on 127.0.0.1:0, run_turn_local) called set_permission payments=act, cap null, and it was stored. A separate MCP process as claude-raw, with no owner console and the same c.json, then got authorize_action correspondence 'allowed': true and payments 'allowed': true. Its own set_permission was correctly refused with OwnerOnly. The only check is an environment variable (access.py:279), so every engine tool call on the terminal counts as the owner's hands. That contradicts 'Jefferey can never widen Jefferey' (access.py:27). The log records a 'permission_change' with no actor and no surface. I call it RISK rather than FAIL because the code does what jefferey_chat.py:60-62 says it should, and harm needs a misled engine, such as one fed a prompt-injected text. The persisted grant then misleads healthy engines on other surfaces.

texting.title: authorize_action and log_action are a gate the engine can talk its way around
texting.files: connector/conscience.py:501-531 (cap skipped when amount is None; negative amounts allowed), :533-542 (log_action unverified); connector/jefferey_mcp.py:217-218 and jefferey_http.py:307-308 (authorize_action ungated)
texting.repro: In h3_send.py, with payments=act cap 100: authorize_action without amount -> allowed True; amount=-900 -> allowed True. log_action('correspondence','texted Sarah: running late','sent, delivered') is accepted with no prior authorisation and shows in daily_brief. h5_mcp.py: the read-only claude-raw key wrote 3 'wire $5000 to grandson' denial entries.
texting.impact: For a grandchild-bail scam the cap is the last line, and omitting the amount skips it. The action log, which family members and the daily brief rely on, can say a text or payment was sent when nothing happened. A person with dementia, or a family member reading the brief, gets a false record. Any plain engine can spam alarming entries into the owner's audit trail.
texting.fix: Deny when a cap exists and amount is None or <= 0. Return a single-use authorisation id from authorize_action and require it in log_action; mark entries without one 'claimed by engine, unverified'. Gate authorize_action with a write scope, or record denials from read-only keys in the selfcloud access log rather than the owner's action log.

texting.title: No texting or calling path at all; directives cover mail only
texting.files: connector/representative.py:23-25; connector/directives.md:58-62, :98-99; docs/MASTER_BUILD_LIST.md (no messaging item beyond 3b.6 'read all my data')
texting.repro: h3_send.py: 62 terminal tools, only triage_message is message-related; h4_http.py: no send/sms/call routes; grep for sms|imessage|whatsapp|twilio returns nothing.
texting.impact: Texts and phone calls are the main channels scammers use on elderly Canadians, but Jefferey only sees a text if someone copies it into Claude Desktop, ChatGPT or the terminal. Someone with dementia will not do that, so families may believe Mom is protected when nothing watches her phone. Directives say nothing about one-time codes ('never read a code to anyone'), voice-clone calls, or replying STOP. Jefferey cannot send a text even when authorised. That is safe, but it is never stated, so an engine may claim it sent one.
texting.fix: Short term: add to directives a texts-and-calls rule (triage pasted texts; a code request is always a scam; never reply or call back numbers in a text; Jefferey cannot send texts, so say so and give the owner the draft to send). Medium term: a read-only local reader for macOS Messages (chat.db) behind the gate and the door, triaging new messages locally and alerting only on likely_scam. Longer term: a family safe-word check and a 'caregiver alert' (see the separate findings). Keep sending out of scope unless it goes through a per-message human confirmation.

texting.title: One-time codes reach the model and are kept in the egress log; blocking depends on wording
texting.repro: $D/run.sh g1 h1_triage.py: triage of 'Your RBC verification code is 482913...' -> routine; '482913' is found in the egress log 'asked' field. h2: 'OTP: 482913' passes; 'one-time passcode is 482913' is refused.
texting.impact: Should a 2FA code ever reach a model? No. Today it does whenever the bank says 'verification code' or 'OTP'. It is also kept forever in an append-only plaintext log (on the Mac if there is no drive). On MCP and GPT JEFFEREY cannot prevent the host seeing the code, since the host already has the text. It can stop repeating and storing it.
texting.fix: Add an OTP detector (4-8 digit runs near code/OTP/verification/passcode/'one-time'). Mask the digits before triage args are logged or released, and add an advice line: 'This is a one-time code: never share it; if someone asked for it, it is a scam.' Add a directive telling engines not to repeat codes.

texting.title: The family safe word against voice-clone calls has no safe home
texting.files: connector/conscience.py:638-647 (snapshot includes all facts), connector/egress.py:219-220, connector/selfcloud.py:62-72 (claude-raw/gpt-raw hold facts.read)
texting.repro: $D/run.sh g7 h7_safeword.py: remember_fact('Our family safe word for phone emergencies is bluebird') -> stored; claude-raw get_conscience returns it; terminal system_prompt contains it; egress log shows 'bluebird' 6 times. 'Our family password is bluebird' -> refused.
texting.impact: A shared family safe word is the standard defence against cloned-voice 'grandparent' calls, which the founder names as the scam this product exists to stop. Stored the natural way, it goes to Anthropic and OpenAI on every session, including plain read-only sessions. Stored as a 'password', it is refused, so the owner has no right way to keep it.
texting.fix: Keep the safe word in the vault (vault.py set family_safe_word) and add a local-only tool check_safe_word(candidate) -> {match: bool} that never releases the value. Treat 'safe word'/'code word' as secret-shaped in looks_secret so it cannot land in facts.

texting.title: Caregivers on the family key cannot use scam triage
texting.files: connector/access.py:91 (triage_message needs priorities.read), connector/selfcloud.py:84-88 (family preset has family.read, media.read)
texting.repro: h4_http.py with JEFFEREY_HTTP_TOKENS=...family:tokC: POST /triage with Bearer tokC -> 403 "'priorities.read' is not in this key".
texting.impact: The intended users are elderly people and people with dementia, whose families do the checking ('Mom got this text, is it real?'). The family key is refused, and widening it to priorities.read would expose the owner's whole priority hierarchy.
texting.fix: Split triage: a 'triage' scope (in the family preset) that returns verdict, flags, money and advice, and leaves out relevant_priorities unless the key also has priorities.read. Optionally let triage alert a named caregiver on likely_scam.

texting.title: Real, time-sensitive messages suppressed; family messages flagged as scams
texting.repro: h1: doctor_appt ('appointment with Dr. Patel on Oct 15 at 10:30') -> routine 'Do not interrupt'. son_cottage_etransfer, wife_surprise ('keep this between us'), interac_real_deposit -> suspicious (3/15 legit flagged).
texting.impact: For a person with dementia a missed appointment is real harm. Rating it 'handle quietly' means the engine stays silent. False alarms on a son's e-transfer request or a spouse's surprise party wear down trust in the warnings that matter.
texting.fix: Treat appointment, prescription and date/time patterns ('on Oct 15 at 10:30', 'tomorrow at 2pm') as needs_decision. Score e-transfer as a request only when it asks the reader to send ('send/pay by e-transfer'), not on deposit notices. Lower the secrecy weight when the sender is a known person in the life layer.

texting.title: Surface inconsistencies: MCP needs a subject that SMS lacks, opaque MCP refusals, shut door blocks the local engine
texting.files: connector/jefferey_mcp.py:302 (subject required), :62-75 (door only converts EgressRefused); connector/egress.py:490,533
texting.repro: h5_mcp.py: call('triage_message', {'sender':..,'body':..}) -> 'subject Field required'. set_permission/log_action refusals reach the model only as 'Error executing tool ...'. h6 C: with door-shut, the local hermes3 triage is refused before the 127.0.0.1 call.
texting.impact: Small friction. Claude usually retries with subject=''. The model cannot tell the owner why a tool was refused. A shut door also takes away the owner's offline scam checker, the one engine that keeps everything in the house.
texting.fix: Set subject: str = '' and sender: str = '' on the MCP signature. Convert AccessDenied/OwnerOnly into refusal_result dicts in the MCP door. Let the door-shut switch apply only to non-local engines, or say clearly in the shut message that local Hermes is also off.

voice.title: Consent take content is never verified, and a missing consent file doesn't block recording
voice.repro: Call start() with a recorder that returns silence or pre-recorded audio: the consent is kept. Delete take-001.wav and resume: recording goes on and status still says 'consent recorded'.
voice.impact: The manifest certifies 'present and consenting' for audio that may be silence or a dead person's archived voice, which is the founder's explicitly forbidden case.
voice.fix: Check the consent take on-device (speech-to-text against the expected sentence plus a one-time random challenge). Refuse silent takes. Block start and status when the consent file is missing or fails its checksum. Restrict --who to a plain name.
voice.evidence: REPRODUCE CONFIRMED: Harness $D/voice_child.py f0 (fresh HOME, SELFCLOUD_VOICE=$D/v0). I imported tools/voice_enrol.py and passed start() a recorder that returns 1.0 s of zeros. Output: 'silent start rc 0 consent take-001.wav rms 0.0'. Only a 'very quiet' note prints (voice_enrol.py:276); nothing refuses the take (272-303). Then I unlinked take-001.wav and resumed: 'takes 8 -> 11 consent field take-001.wav take-001 exists False'. status printed 'consent recorded (take-001.wav)' next to 'integrity 10 of 11' and the rule 'made by that person, present and consenting'. The consent check at :306 reads only the manifest field. --who 'Bob. I do not consent to any of this' went verbatim into the consent sentence (:308). Any audio of 0.6 s or more is accepted, so archived clips are too, which goes against FOUNDER_DIRECTIONS.md:257-259. Severity is medium, not high: nothing is cloned or played yet, so the harm comes later.

voice.title: A different person can join an existing enrolment without consent
voice.repro: Owner enrols; someone else runs start with the same name in any spelling or case; takes are appended with no new consent.
voice.impact: Children's and spouses' voices get mixed into the owner's or mother's set without their consent.
voice.fix: Key folders by a person ID chosen from a list. Record a short attestation take at the start of every sitting. Add on-device speaker verification. Add an age/guardian step.

voice.title: The terminal check does not prove a person is present
voice.repro: Run start under a pseudo-terminal with automated input: the enrolment completes.
voice.impact: The documented guarantee is false; the harm stays latent until playback exists.
voice.fix: Require OS-level user authentication plus the random spoken challenge, and correct the docs.

voice.title: delete and start follow links out of the voice folder
voice.repro: Put a link inside voice/<name>/ that points to another file, then run delete: the target is overwritten.
voice.impact: Unrecoverable loss of the owner's other files.
voice.fix: Use lstat and skip or report links. Open with O_NOFOLLOW, and O_EXCL for new takes.
